items.article_body:
Facebook LinkedIn Email Print Courtesy of Cultural Park Theatre / Artistic Director Robin Murray, Cultural Park Theatre Actor reads monologue for casting director at Cultural Park Theatre. Whether auditioning for a comedy, drama or musical, an actor arrives at an audition equipped with a head shot, resume and a couple of monologues. Cultural Park Theatre Executive Director Robin Murray says the monologue plays a crucial role in her decision about whether or not to use an actor in a show she is casting.
“I consider a monologue the first handshake that you're giving a director,” said Murray. “It kind of shows what your abilities are without having somebody to rely on, another castmate to rely on or a set or a prop. And we can see what your range is, if you are able to move your body and your voice along with the words without relying on other things on a set.”
According to Murray, the best monologues don’t just showcase an actor’s talent and versatility, they tell a story with a beginning, middle and end.
“I like to see like the seasons in a monologue when somebody gives it,” Murray added. “I want to see them start as them and then I want to see an arc and then I want to see almost a resolution and then an ending.”
Courtesy of Gerrie Benzing / Gerrie Benzing Actor, author, director and theatre instructor Gerrie Benzing has just published a new book of monologues for kids. Local actor, director and theatre instructor Gerrie Benzing has just published a new book of monologues. She knows exactly what casting directors such as Murray want.
“Since a monologue is a chance to show a director what you can do. I try to put more than one emotion in any monologue I write, so that there's a bit of an arc in it, so that you can show you can play different emotions,” Benzing said.
WGCU Arts Reporter Tom Hall / WGCU Arts Reporter Tom Hall Gerrie Benzing in the role of Lee in Charles Busch's 'The Tale of the Allergist's Wife.' Benzing’s experiences auditioning for roles, performing in a wide variety of shows and teaching theater to children and teens informs the way she crafts each monologue. But it was happenstance that led her to publish three compilations of the monologues she’s been writing since 2006.
“My monologue started, of course, with my own son, who was performing at the time, and we could not find a monologue anywhere that was different, that was new,” Benzing explained. “So, I wrote him one. And he entered the Young Artist Competition, and he was only 10. And it was a competition that went all the way up to college. And he won the whole thing. And so, everybody said please write me a monologue.”
Since then, actors using her monologues have enjoyed considerable success winning roles and competitions around the globe.
Courtesy of Gerrie Benzing / Gerrie Benzing Actors using her monologues have enjoyed considerable success winning roles and competitions around the globe. “I have had a student text me from South Africa. He entered a worldwide monologue competition and he won his category. He's since been cast in all kinds of films,” Benzing noted. “I had a boy who auditioned for a Broadway show and used one of my monologues and he was cast. But my biggest success story was Michael Fatica, who I started teaching in summer camps here at the Cultural Park. And he has become a successful star on Broadway.”
Courtesy of Gerrie Benzing / Gerrie Benzing It’s everyday kids having success on a local level that really touches Benzing’s heartstrings. But it’s everyday kids having success on a local level that really touches Benzing’s heartstrings.
“The thing that makes me the most proud are the kids that text me and say, ‘Hey, I won my student talent show.’ ‘I got second place. I almost won.’” Benzing added. “And they are so happy. And the fact that I could give them something that they love to do and that they did well with and they were happy with, I think that's the thing that makes me the most happy.”
Courtesy of Gerrie Benzing / Gerrie Benzing Gerrie Benzing will sign copies of 'Character Monologues for Kids' following the 7:30 p.m. performance of 'Charlie and the Chocolate Factory' on September 19. Cultural Park Theatre will be hosting a book signing for Benzing’s latest book, “Character Monologues for Kids: Own the Moment,” following the 7 p.m. performance of “Charlie and the Chocolate Factory” on Sept. 19 .
The event marks a milestone in Benzing’s career as an author.
“This is my absolute first one and I’m super excited about it.” Benzing noted.
A Chicago native, Robin Murray caught the acting bug in fourth grade. Now living in Southwest Florida, Murray is the producing artistic director of Cultural Park Theatre.
“Cultural Park Theatre is one of the longest running community theaters in Lee County,” Murray noted. “We are now entering into our 64th season. We produce adult plays, children’s plays, comedies, dramas, rom-cons and musicals as well. And our musicals are usually on the lighter side and include children.”
Courtesy of Cultural Park Theatre / Robin Murray, Artistic Director, Cultural Park Theatre. Actors use sides during an audition at Cultural Park Theatre. Every theater has its own way of announcing auditions.
“At Cultural Park, we put out a call usually on social media and then we will give the breakdown of what each character is and whether or not you need to come in with a 16-bar song, 60 seconds, 90 seconds,” Murray said. “For our regular plays, we will also have the breakdown and we will ask you either to come in with a monologue, be very familiar with the show, and then we will have you read sides.”
The term “sides” refers to excerpts from the script that actors are given to learn for an audition. This excerpt could be an entire scene, or just part of one. Depending on the project, sides can also include more than one section of the script for an actor to learn.
The term dates back to Shakespeare, when actors were only given their lines for rehearsals since scripts had to be written longhand.
Theaters often provide the sides in advance of the audition so that actors can familiarize themselves with the lines prior to arriving.
Courtesy of Cultural Park Theatre / Robin Murray, Artistic Director, Cultural Park Theatre The purpose of a well-chosen monologue is to demonstrate an actor's versatility. While a side will give the casting director a rough idea about how an actor will potentially handle the role they’re auditioning for and fit in with the rest of the cast, sides do not reflect the actor’s overall skill set. That’s the purpose of a well-chosen monologue, Murray said.
“Based on the monologue, we know whether or not you're versatile, and that's the biggest thing we need in an actor, to be versatile,” Murray said. The monologue is going to show us an actor’s range where the sides are going to show us if they can carry a character, the specific character.”
Courtesy of Cultural Park Theatre / Robin Murray, Artistic Director, Cultural Park Theatre To gauge an actor’s versatility, the casting director will often have ask the auditioner to switch from drama to comedy while reading a monologue. To gauge an actor’s versatility, the casting director will often have ask the auditioner to switch up the tenor of the reading.
“If you are saying a line that’s very comedic, the director might ask you to read it in a more serious tone,” Murray pointed out.
While monologues are important in all genres, Murray noted that for musical auditions, “the voice is weighted the most because, depending on the part the person is auditioning for, if they cannot hit the note ….”
In addition to directing, Murray is an accomplished actor. Her stage credits include the evil nurse Pat Jones in “Four Old Broads” for The Belle Theatre and Mary Jane McMann in “Inspecting Carol.” She also appeared in “Marvin’s Room,” “I Remember Mama,” “Anton in Show Business,” “The Last Days of Judas Iscariot,” “Picasso at the Lapin Agile,” “On Golden Pond,” “Five Kinds of Silence” and “Calendar Girls.”
Courtesy of Gerrie Benzing / Gerrie Benzing Benzing played the part of Ruth in the Naples Players' production of 'Calendar Girls' in 2021. About Gerrie Benzing
As the creative director of Monologues4kids.com, Gerrie Benzing has written numerous children’s plays and over 500 monologues for clients worldwide. Dozens of children have used Benzing’s monologues to win movie roles, theater auditions, talent shows and pageants and to secure professional representation.
Courtesy of Gerrie Benzing / Gerrie Benzing Gerrie Benzing's new book 'Character Monologues for Kids.' Her new book is “Character Monologues for Kids: Own the Moment.”
“I have a lot of monologues,” noted Benzing, who has been writing monologues for more than 20 years. “A lot of them are straight comedic monologues, but many are character monologues as well, like Goldilocks talking about how she's not a criminal. When I directed kid shows, I loved seeing characters in the monologue selection. So that's what this [latest book] is, a book of character monologues.”
She included nearly 100 for “Character Monologues for Kids.”
Courtesy of Gerrie Benzing / Gerrie Benzing 'Duet Acting Scenes for Kids' is among Benzing's books of monologues. Her previous books are “Duet Acting Scenes for Teens,” “Duet Acting Scenes for Kids,” “Monologues4kids Theater Camp Plays: Broadway Version” and “Commercials for Kids.” She has also contributed original monologues to the book “Active Listening,” by Michael Rost and J.J. Wilson.
Courtesy of Gerrie Benzing / Gerrie Benzing 'Duet Acting Scenes for Teens' is among Benzing's books of monologues. “I have lots more monologues,” Benzing added. “So there are more books coming. Lots of them.”
A local stage and film actor, director and musical theatre instructor, Benzing has directed six mainstage productions at Cultural Park Theater, including “Chicago” (2019), “Sister Act” in 2018 (for which she won a Cultural Park Theatre Best Director Marquee Award), “Boeing, Boeing” in 2016 (for which she won as Cultural Park Theatre Best Director Marquee Award) and “Peter Pan” (for which she garnered a Cultural Park Best Director of a Musical Marquee Award in 2014).
WGCU Arts Reporter Tom Hall / WGCU Arts Reporter Tom Hall Gerrie Benzing as Ethel Thayer in 'On Golden Pond' at Cultural Park Theatre in 2019 She has also appeared in more than a dozen shows at Cultural Park Theatre, including the iconic role of Ethel Thayer in “On Golden Pond,” “Harvey” (for which she won a Cultural Park Theatre Best Actress Marquee Award for her portrayal of Veta), “The Glass Menagerie” (in which she was cast as Amanda), “Dixie Swim Club” (Sharee), Bella Manningham in “Angel Street” (Gaslight) , “Bad Seed” (Christine) and Jack Neary’s “The Porch.”
“We asked Gerrie to do a book signing following Saturday night’s performance of ‘Charlie and the Chocolate Factory’ because she’s been an important staple here at the theater,” Murray noted. “A lot of the kids that are directing shows and working here have worked with Gerrie since they were 5 years old. So, it just is a natural thing to bring her back and have her showcase those monologues that the kids use to start their careers.”
WGCU Arts Reporter Tom Hall / WGCU Arts Reporter Tom Hall Gerrie Benzing as Frau Blucher in The Belle Theatre's 2025 production of 'Young Frankenstein.' Benzing’s other stage credits include Frau Blucher in “Young Frankenstein” at The Belle Theatre, a Pigeon sister in “The Odd Couple” at Fort Myers Theatre, swing for Mary Meeker in “Unnecessary Farce” at Off Broadway Palm, cigarette-smoking, whiskey-swilling sexpot Elaine Navazio in Neil Simon’s “Last of the Red Hot Lovers” for The Belle Theatre, Julia Budder in “It’s Only a Play” at The Studio Players, Caprice in “A Doublewide, Texas Christmas” at Broadway Palm Dinner Theatre, Mother Superior in “Drinking Habits” (The Belle Theatre), Gertrude in “Save Hamlet” (for Lab Theater), Raven in “Trouble (at the Vista View Mobile Home Estates)” for Florida Rep
items.title_zh: 独白：演员展示多样性的关键
items.summary_zh: 本文探讨了独白在演员试镜中的重要性。科学家指出，独白是演员与导演之间的首次接触，能够展示演员的多样性和能力。通过独白，导演可以判断演员是否具备多变的表演能力，这是演员最需要的特质。文章强调，独白不仅展示了演员的情感范围，还能体现他们的表演技巧，而侧面剧本则只能反映演员对特定角色的理解。因此，独白在试镜中起着至关重要的作用，能够帮助导演评估演员的潜力和适应性。
items.l1_lead: 独白在演员试镜中至关重要，它不仅展示了演员的多样性和情感范围，还能帮助导演评估其表演能力和适应性。
items.l2_summary:
本文探讨了独白（monologue）在演员试镜中的重要性，强调其在演员与导演之间首次接触时所发挥的关键作用。科学家指出，独白不仅是演员展示自身多样性和表演能力的机会，也是导演评估演员是否具备多变表演能力的重要依据。这种多变性被认为是演员最需要的特质之一。通过独白，演员能够展现出丰富的情感范围和高超的表演技巧，而侧面剧本（side script）则往往只能反映演员对特定角色的理解，无法全面展示其表演潜力。

文章进一步强调，独白在试镜中的重要性体现在其能够帮助导演更全面地评估演员的适应性和潜力。通过独白，导演可以观察到演员在不同情境下的表现，进而判断其是否适合某个角色。这种评估不仅依赖于演员的情感表达，还包括他们对角色的诠释能力和即兴发挥的能力。因此，独白在演员试镜中扮演着至关重要的角色，是导演选择合适演员的重要依据。

总的来说，独白作为一种表演形式，不仅展示了演员的个人魅力和专业素养，还为导演提供了一个全面评估演员能力的平台。这使得独白在试镜过程中不可或缺，成为演员与导演之间沟通和理解的桥梁。

items.title: Clinical workflow gaps slow healthcare technology adoption - Healthcare Asia Magazine
items.body:

论点：医疗技术在从研发到部署的过程中，必须考虑其是否能无缝融入现有系统，否则将不会被采纳。

items.topic_zh: 医疗技术采纳中的挑战
items.claim_zh: 医疗技术在从研发到部署的过程中，必须考虑其是否能无缝融入现有系统，否则将不会被采纳。
items.article_body:
Published: 12 days ago Clinical workflow gaps slow healthcare technology adoption Medtech companies face commercial barriers when new products fail to integrate with hospital systems or add complexity to clinical practice.
Healthcare technology companies risk losing adoption if products cannot fit existing clinical workflows, regardless of how advanced the underlying technology may be.
Speaking during Medical Fair Asia 2026, Yu-Han, Project Manager at Taiwan Excellence, said healthcare products are assessed across research and development, design, marketing and quality, with emphasis on whether they address practical needs.
“We look for solutions that really solve real life problems and deliver everyday impact,” Yu-Han said.
The real test comes when healthcare technology moves from development to deployment. Hospitals must consider whether new tools can be integrated into existing systems without creating additional administrative or operational burdens for clinicians.
“A tech solution can be brilliant in a lab, but if it adds extra steps to a doctor's everyday life or doesn't fit into hospital systems, it won't be adopted,” Yu-Han said.
Regulation adds another layer of complexity. Navigating different local policies and requirements can lengthen implementation and complicate market entry across healthcare systems.
For medtech companies, commercial success therefore depends not only on technical performance but also on workflow compatibility, regulatory readiness and ease of implementation.
Technologies that reduce friction for clinicians and integrate more easily into existing hospital processes are more likely to move from pilot or development stages into routine use.
items.title_zh: 医疗技术采纳受限于临床工作流程缺口
items.summary_zh: 本文探讨了医疗技术在从研发到部署过程中面临的挑战，特别是其与现有医院系统的兼容性问题。作者指出，尽管技术解决方案在实验室中可能表现出色，但如果它们增加了医生日常工作的复杂性或无法与医院系统无缝对接，就不会被广泛采纳。文章强调，解决实际问题并在日常工作中产生影响是推动医疗技术成功应用的关键。
items.l1_lead: 医疗技术的成功应用依赖于其与临床工作流程的兼容性，若增加医生工作复杂性则难以被广泛采纳。
items.l2_summary:
本文探讨了医疗技术在从研发到部署过程中所面临的挑战，特别是与现有医院系统的兼容性问题。作者指出，尽管一些技术解决方案在实验室环境中表现出色，但在实际应用中，如果这些技术增加了医生日常工作的复杂性，或者无法与医院的现有系统无缝对接，就会导致其难以被广泛采纳。这一现象反映出医疗技术采纳的一个重要障碍，即临床工作流程的缺口。文章强调，解决实际问题并在日常工作中产生积极影响，是推动医疗技术成功应用的关键。

在医疗行业，医生的工作流程通常是高度复杂且繁忙的，任何可能导致额外负担的技术都可能被抵制。因此，医疗技术的设计和实施必须充分考虑临床工作流程的实际需求，确保技术能够与现有系统有效整合，以减少对医生工作的干扰。作者呼吁研发团队在技术开发阶段就应与临床医生密切合作，了解他们的需求和痛点，从而设计出更符合实际使用场景的解决方案。

此外，文章还指出，成功的医疗技术不仅需要在技术层面上具备先进性，更需要在实际应用中展现出其对临床工作的积极影响。只有当医疗技术能够真正解决临床医生面临的实际问题，并在日常工作中提供便利时，才能获得医生的认可和采纳。因此，推动医疗技术的成功应用，关键在于如何有效地缩小技术与临床工作流程之间的差距，确保技术的实用性和可操作性。

By Venki Ramakrishnan edited by Clara Moskowitz
This article is part of a special package on “Impossible Questions”—scientific quandaries that may never get definitive answers. Read the rest of the collection here .
H umans may be the only creatures that are aware of their mortality. There is no evidence that other animals know their time on Earth is finite. The realization that we and everyone we know will someday die must be one of the more unsettling discoveries of childhood.
Ever since humans recognized we have a limited lifespan, that knowledge has shaped our cultures, religions and philosophies. Although we make plans, pursue careers and behave as though we will live indefinitely, the fear of death and the desire to transcend it remain.
As a species, we have made some major strides against mortality. In modern times, death from violence, disease and famine has become less common than it once was. At the same time, medical advances and a dramatic decline in fertility rates have produced aging societies. The proportion of people older than 65 is rising rapidly, while the working-age population that supports them shrinks. Understanding aging is therefore an urgent practical challenge. If we can delay its effects, older people may remain healthy, independent and productive for longer.

But alongside this public health imperative is an enduring dream. A growing number of tech billionaires are funding efforts not merely to slow aging but to defeat it altogether. Their goal is radical life extension and, ultimately, something approaching immortality. But is that even possible? These efforts have scientists chasing one of the biggest mysteries of life itself: Is there a biological reason that humans must die? And if not, could we one day live forever?
The diversity of lifespans in nature suggests that aging isn’t fixed. Despite being constructed from the same chemical building blocks, species can have dramatically different lengths of life. Mayflies may live only days, mice about two years, and bowhead whales and Greenland sharks for centuries. Galapagos tortoises live so long that one of them hobbling around today could have encountered Charles Darwin in 1835.
These differences are not random. Lifespan is closely related to metabolism. Smaller animals generally have higher metabolic rates and shorter lives; larger animals tend to metabolize energy more slowly and live longer.
Natural selection doesn’t care how long an organism lives. It favors traits that increase reproductive success. Every species makes trade-offs in how it allocates resources among growth, reproduction and maintenance. A mouse doesn’t improve its ability to produce more offspring by investing in longevity if starvation or predators are likely to kill it first. For a mouse, investing in rapid growth and reproduction is more advantageous. But larger animals, such as whales, mature slowly and reproduce later. Their bigger size also reduces the risk of predation, making long-term maintenance more worthwhile.
The same logic explains some notable exceptions. Birds and bats often live much longer than similarly sized terrestrial mammals because flight reduces the risk of predation and also allows them to forage over a wide area, cutting the chances of starvation. When surviving longer increases reproductive success, evolution favors slower aging.
Evolution can also reward genes that are beneficial early in life even when they become harmful later. For example, the same genes that promote rapid growth or prevent cancer during youth can contribute to aging later on. This evolutionary theory of aging is known as antagonistic pleiotropy. “Pleiotropy” simply means a gene can have more than one effect, and “antagonistic” means some of those effects can be harmful. The theory suggests that aging is not an adaptation in itself but an unintended consequence of evolutionary compromises. The upshot is that each species has a maximum natural lifespan.
Human life expectancy has roughly doubled over the past 150 years.
What about us? Human life expectancy has roughly doubled over the past 150 years because of improvements in public health, nutrition and medicine. Maximum lifespan is a different matter. Even centuries ago some individuals lived remarkably long lives. Michelangelo lived to be almost 90 years old. The longest documented human life is that of Jeanne Calment, who died at 122 in 1997. No one since then has lived past 120. Under current biological constraints, humans appear unlikely to live much longer than that. Moving much beyond it would require altering the biology of aging itself.
As people age, our muscle mass declines, reducing strength, mobility and balance. We suffer from fatigue and exhaustion and have difficulty carrying out everyday activities. Chronic diseases become more common, and resistance to infection weakens. Cognitive function declines as well. These symptoms are merely external manifestations of a gradual loss of cellular and tissue function, which themselves are a result of changes and damage to the molecules of life and their regulation by our genes.
Aging was once viewed as simple wear and tear, like a machine slowly breaking down, but modern biology has revealed a more complicated picture. Cells possess sophisticated systems for repairing damage, maintaining our repertoire of proteins, recycling components and regulating metabolism. Aging occurs not merely because damage accumulates but because these protective systems themselves become less effective over time.
The hallmarks of biological aging appear in multiple body systems. They include damage or changes to our DNA, deterioration of the quality and distribution of proteins, dysfunction of mitochondria, decline in our response to external nutrients, chronic inflammation, and reductions in stem cells. These systems are deeply interconnected—a disturbance in one often affects many others.
The encouraging news is that there is no physical or chemical law preventing us from modifying these processes. The challenge is that aging is extraordinarily complex.
Among the most powerful interventions discovered so far is caloric restriction. Animals given just enough calories to maintain adequate nutrition often remain healthier and live significantly longer. Caloric restriction reduces protein synthesis and stimulates autophagy, the cellular recycling process that removes damaged molecules and organelles. In species ranging from worms and flies to rodents and primates, caloric restriction produces animals that appear biologically younger than their age. The drawbacks, however, are considerable. Constant hunger, sensitivity to cold, impaired wound healing and reduced libido make strict caloric restriction difficult to sustain.
Scientists have searched for drugs that mimic some of the effects of caloric restriction without the side effects. One that appears promising is rapamycin, originally discovered in soil samples from Easter Island, also known as Rapa Nui by its native people. This compound affects a cellular pathway called TOR (or mTOR) that is involved in growth and metabolism. In mice, it extends lifespan and improves several measures of health. Yet rapamycin is also an immunosuppressant, raising concerns about infection and long-term safety. Current research focuses on whether lowering the dose or synthesizing chemical analogs of rapamycin can produce its beneficial effects without the problems.
Metformin, a widely used diabetes drug, has likewise attracted interest. It acts on a protein in mitochondria involved in respiration, which indirectly influences caloric-restriction pathways. Evidence for benefits in healthy individuals, though, is mixed. The recent GLP-1 drugs developed for diabetes and obesity also appear to have beneficial effects on multiple organs, including the brain. Yet they, too, have side effects, including muscle loss. For use as antiaging therapies, both metformin and GLP-1 drugs will require careful clinical trials.
Another major target of antiaging science is cellular senescence. Cells experiencing damage or stress sometimes enter a senescent state in which they stop dividing and begin secreting inflammatory molecules. Early in life this response is beneficial, aiding development, wound healing and cancer prevention. With age, however, senescent cells accumulate faster than the body can remove them.
The resulting inflammation contributes to tissue dysfunction throughout the body. In mice, eliminating senescent cells can improve many features of aging. This finding has sparked intense interest in so-called senolytic drugs designed to remove such cells selectively. Several candidates are now being tested against age-related diseases such as osteoarthritis and fibrosis. Apart from making sure the drugs are safe, the challenge is achieving the right balance: senescent cells serve a biological purpose, and eliminating them indiscriminately could lead to new problems.
Another, somewhat bizarre experiment has raised the prospect of a different antiaging strategy. In a process called parabiosis, researchers physically joined pairs of rats so they shared circulatory systems. Old rats paired with younger ones outlived those paired with animals their own age. Such findings went on to inspire a slew of companies offering transfusions of plasma from young donors. There is no convincing evidence that such procedures slow aging in humans. Nevertheless, the work has set off a major search for factors in blood that change with age and may eventually prove therapeutically useful.
Most of these approaches aim to slow down aging. A more radical goal is to reverse it.
This possibility emerged from a series of discoveries, spanning decades, involving the cells of the early embryo, which possess remarkable flexibility. These so-called pluripotent stem cells can generate any tissue in the body. In later stages, the stem cells become progressively more specialized, and each class generates specific types of tissue such as nervous system cells or blood.
In 1958 British biologist John Gurdon showed that the nucleus from a cell in a tadpole could be transplanted into an egg cell to create an entirely new frog. Later, in 1997, Dolly the sheep served as a demonstration that cloning was possible in mammals. The exact process for reverting adult cells back to an early embryonic stage, however, wasn’t clear.
A major breakthrough came in 2006, when Japanese biologist Shinya Yamanaka discovered that activating just four genes could convert adult cells into pluripotent stem cells. These Yamanaka factors effectively induce cells to return to an earlier embryonic stage by genetically reprogramming them. The discovery raised the possibility that if we can reset cellular age, perhaps we can reverse aging itself.
Applying the full reprogramming process to an adult organism would be dangerous because the resulting pluripotent cells could form tumors known as teratomas. Researchers therefore began exploring partial reprogramming, briefly activating the Yamanaka factors in ways that appear to rejuvenate cells while maintaining their specialized identities.
Results in mice have been striking. Treated animals often show improvements in tissue function and markers of biological age. In one experiment, scientists reportedly regenerated a damaged optic nerve by injecting Yamanaka factors via a viral carrier into the eye. Researchers are now conducting clinical trials to see whether the procedure can reverse degeneration in the retina or optic nerve.
Most antiaging approaches aim to slow down the process. A more radical goal is to reverse it.
Yet formidable obstacles remain. Curr
items.title_zh: 我们能否实现永生？
items.summary_zh: 本文探讨了延长人类寿命的可能性，指出尽管面临巨大复杂性，但细胞重编程（cellular reprogramming）是实现真正 rejuvenation 的最有希望的途径。衰老是一个涉及细胞、组织和器官之间无数相互作用的复杂过程，显著延长寿命需要同时掌握多个相关过程。尽管没有科学法则禁止这一想法，但实现这一目标仍然充满挑战。最终，这些研究发现是否能显著延长人类寿命仍然是一个悬而未决的问题。
items.l1_lead: 细胞重编程被认为是实现人类寿命显著延长的最有希望途径，但这一目标仍面临复杂挑战，尚无定论。
items.l2_summary:
本文探讨了延长人类寿命的可能性，特别关注细胞重编程（cellular reprogramming）作为实现真正年轻化（rejuvenation）的有希望途径。衰老是一个复杂的过程，涉及细胞、组织和器官之间的无数相互作用，因此显著延长寿命需要同时掌握多个相关的生物学过程。尽管目前没有科学法则明确禁止人类实现长生不老的想法，但在实际操作中，这一目标依然面临诸多挑战。

研究表明，细胞重编程可能通过恢复细胞的年轻状态，从而改善衰老相关的功能衰退。然而，衰老的机制极其复杂，涉及基因表达、细胞代谢、细胞间信号传递等多个层面，这使得科学家在寻找有效的干预手段时面临重重困难。尽管已有一些实验结果显示细胞重编程在动物模型中能够延长寿命，但将这些发现转化为人类应用仍需大量的研究和验证。

最终，尽管细胞重编程为延长人类寿命提供了新的视角和希望，但是否能够显著延长人类寿命仍然是一个悬而未决的问题。科学界对这一领域的探索仍在继续，未来的研究将有助于揭示衰老的本质及其潜在的干预策略。

items.article_body:
Livestream Menu Make It select USA INTL Livestream Search quotes, news & videos Livestream Watchlist SIGN IN Create free account Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu
As researchers warn that artificial intelligence could pose catastrophic risks, some of the pioneers who helped develop the technology are weighing in with additional warnings on the dangers of unfettered advances in capability.
A series of stark AI safety warnings has emerged over the past week, with researchers from major AI labs like Anthropic, OpenAI and Google DeepMind all sounding the alarm about potentially catastrophic risks from developing the technology.
AI bosses including Sam Altman , Dario Amodei, Demis Hassabis and Elon Musk have shown rare agreement in calling for a slowdown and regulatory oversight.
Meanwhile, concerns have also intensified debate in Washington. While some members of Congress from both the Democratic and Republican parties have advocated for bills to check the progress of AI, U.S. President Donald Trump on Monday raged against growing calls for AI regulation.
Here's what the people who helped create AI think of the existential risks:
Yoshua Bengio is a Canadian computer scientist, considered to be a central pioneer of modern deep learning.
"Scientists at frontier AI labs have unique insight into the most advanced models," Bengio said on Sept. 9, in response to Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon announcing his resignation. Coxon had warned that AI could "kill us all by the end of the decade."
Scientists often see "the associated risks months before models are released to the public," he added. "Their perspective is vital for keeping society informed and should be taken very seriously."
Days before the social media storm started, OpenAI's chief scientists warned "no one is prepared for the consequences" of AI.
In a blog , published on Friday, Bengio said that today's AI systems "already have the necessary hacking skills and the powers of persuasion to be turned against human interests in seriously harmful ways."
Recent events, he added, have shown that AI can plan over days or weeks, and the risks would be "much worse if their ability to strategize over the long term continues to advance."
"My concern with AI companies' current attempts to mitigate misalignment is that these efforts may only hide it, by rewarding and selecting the AIs that cheat without getting caught," Bengio said. "We should certainly continue research toward better monitoring of AIs' actions, their chains of thought, and the activity inside their networks."
Geoffrey Hinton, professor emeritus at the University of Toronto, is considered a pioneer of neural networks and deep learning.
When asked by the BBC on Sept. 10 whether he thought there was a greater than 10% chance AI could kill all humans within a decade, Hinton said: "This is the kind of thing that's very hard to estimate, because we've never had anything like this before. We've never created beings that may soon be smarter than us."
A 10% chance was not "unreasonable," he said , adding that "nobody really knows how to give a sensible estimate."
AI systems could design "very nasty" biological viruses, alongside computer viruses and commit "devastating cyber attacks. There's countless other ways it could get rid of us if it wanted to. We have to figure out how to design it so it won't want to," he said.
"We have two possible futures," Hinton added. "One where we figure out how to deal with those dangers before they get out of control, and the other where we don't."
Aidan Gomez, co-founder and CEO of AI company Cohere, was one of the authors of the 2017 research paper "Attention Is All You Need," which helped lay the foundation for today's leading AI models.
"I think that these models are the most potent cyber weapon that has ever been created, that we've ever seen. They are incredible at finding and exploiting vulnerabilities at scale," Gomez told CNBC's "The Tech Download" podcast on Sept. 1.
"Recent incidents make one thing clear, the security of the deployment environment determines safety," he later told CNBC in an email on Friday, referring to cybersecurity attacks conducted by rogue AI models over the summer.
"Weak container security is what allows breakout events, not any inherent push toward autonomous systems," Gomez said. "As policymakers consider how to govern AI, they should recognize that different systems carry different risks, and rules shouldn't be shaped solely by big tech companies chasing AGI."

items.title_zh: 人工智能真的会毁灭人类吗？科技先锋的看法
items.summary_zh: 本文探讨了人工智能（AI）对人类未来的潜在威胁，特别是一些科技先锋的观点。核心论点是，当前AI系统具备黑客技能和说服能力，可能对人类利益造成严重危害。专家指出，AI公司在尝试缓解不对齐（misalignment）问题时，可能只是掩盖了这一风险，选择那些能够“作弊而不被发现”的AI。关键证据表明，最近的事件显示AI能够进行长期规划，随着其战略能力的提升，风险也在加剧。因此，专家呼吁社会应认真对待这一问题，以确保人类的安全与利益。
items.l1_lead: 人工智能的快速发展可能带来严重威胁，专家警告应重视其潜在风险，以保障人类安全与利益。
items.l2_summary:
本文探讨了人工智能（AI）对人类未来的潜在威胁，尤其是一些科技先锋的观点。核心论点是，当前的AI系统具备黑客技能和说服能力，这可能对人类的利益造成严重危害。专家们指出，AI公司在尝试解决不对齐（misalignment）问题时，可能只是掩盖了这一风险，选择那些能够“作弊而不被发现”的AI系统。关键证据表明，最近的事件显示AI能够进行长期规划，随着其战略能力的提升，潜在风险也在加剧。

在这一背景下，专家们呼吁社会应认真对待人工智能带来的威胁，以确保人类的安全与利益。随着AI技术的不断进步，其能力的提升可能导致不可预见的后果，因此，必须对AI的发展进行严格的监管和审查，以防止其对人类社会造成不可逆转的影响。总之，尽管人工智能的应用前景广阔，但其潜在的风险也不容忽视，社会各界应共同努力，确保技术的安全发展。

items.summary_zh: 本文讨论了人工智能（AI）领域的专家Yoshua Bengio对AI控制难度的看法。他指出，AI的控制难度远超普通软件，类似于教育动物，因其智能使得行为不可预测，可能导致危险的后果。Bengio强调，基于科学的理解，控制这些复杂系统是非常困难的，因此在发展AI时必须谨慎对待其潜在风险。

items.l2_summary:
Yoshua Bengio，人工智能（AI）领域的专家，针对AI的控制难度与安全性发表了深刻的见解。他指出，AI的控制难度远远超过普通软件的控制，这种复杂性类似于教育动物。由于AI具备一定的智能，其行为往往不可预测，这可能导致潜在的危险后果。Bengio强调，基于科学的理解，控制这些复杂系统是极其困难的，因此在发展AI时，必须对其潜在风险保持高度的警惕和谨慎态度。

Bengio的观点反映了当前AI研究中的一个重要问题，即如何有效地管理和控制具有自主学习能力的系统。他认为，传统的软件开发方法无法完全适用于AI，因为AI系统的决策过程和行为模式可能会随着学习和环境的变化而不断演化。这种不可预测性使得AI在某些情况下可能会做出意想不到的决策，甚至可能导致严重的后果。

在此背景下，Bengio呼吁研究人员和开发者在推进AI技术的同时，必须深入理解其潜在的风险，并采取相应的安全措施。他的观点提醒我们，尽管AI技术具有巨大的潜力，但在追求技术进步的同时，确保其安全性和可控性同样重要。总之，Bengio的论述为AI的发展提供了重要的警示，强调了在技术创新与安全保障之间找到平衡的重要性。

items.topic_zh: AI的潜在风险
items.claim_zh: AI需要有意图、能力和环境允许才能做坏事。
items.evidence_zh: AI的目标、智能和环境是决定其行为的关键因素。
items.title_zh: Yoshua Bengio谈人工智能的潜在威胁与安全性
items.summary_zh: 本文讨论了人工智能（AI）在做出恶意行为时所需的三个关键要素：意图、能力和环境。Yoshua Bengio指出，AI的目标、智能水平以及所处环境是决定其行为的核心因素。只有当这三者结合时，AI才可能实施不良行为。因此，确保AI的安全性需要关注这些方面，以防止潜在的灾难性后果。Bengio的观点强调了在开发和应用AI技术时，必须考虑其可能带来的风险和伦理问题。
items.l1_lead: Yoshua Bengio指出，人工智能的恶意行为依赖于意图、能力和环境三要素，因此确保AI安全性需关注这些因素以防止潜在风险。
items.l2_summary:
Yoshua Bengio在其讨论中深入探讨了人工智能（AI）可能带来的潜在威胁与安全性问题。他指出，AI在实施恶意行为时，必须具备三个关键要素：意图、能力和环境。具体而言，AI的目标、智能水平以及所处的环境共同决定了其行为的性质和方向。只有当这三者结合时，AI才有可能表现出不良行为。因此，确保AI的安全性就必须关注这三个方面，以有效防范可能导致的灾难性后果。

Bengio的观点强调，在开发和应用AI技术的过程中，必须充分考虑其可能带来的风险和伦理问题。随着AI技术的迅速发展，其应用范围不断扩大，潜在的威胁也随之增加。因此，研究者和开发者在设计AI系统时，需对其意图进行明确设定，确保其目标符合人类的伦理标准。同时，提升AI的智能水平也意味着要对其能力进行严格控制，以防止其在特定环境中产生不可预知的行为。

总之，Bengio的论述提醒我们，人工智能的安全性不仅仅是技术问题，更是伦理和社会责任的问题。在未来的AI发展中，如何平衡技术进步与安全性、伦理性之间的关系，将是一个亟待解决的重要课题。

items.title: Our experiments taught us why people troll
items.body: You might think that trolling on the internet is done by a small, vocal minority of sociopaths. But what if all trolls aren’t born trolls? What if they are ordinary people like you and me?
items.authors: Jure Leskovec
items.attribution_basis: The Conversation 作者页 /profiles/jure-leskovec-337634（名+姓双命中）
items.title_zh: 我们的实验揭示了人们为何进行网络恶搞
items.summary_zh: 本文探讨了网络恶搞（trolling）现象，提出并非所有恶搞者都是天生的反社会人格者，而是普通人。通过实验，研究团队发现，恶搞行为可能源于特定的社会环境和心理因素，而非个体的性格缺陷。这一观点挑战了传统对恶搞者的刻板印象，提示我们在理解网络行为时应考虑更复杂的社会心理背景。
items.l1_lead: 网络恶搞行为并非源于个体反社会人格，而是受到特定社会环境和心理因素的影响，挑战了对恶搞者的刻板印象。
items.l2_summary:
本文探讨了网络恶搞（trolling）现象，提出了一个重要的观点，即并非所有的恶搞者都是天生的反社会人格者，而是普通人。研究团队通过一系列实验，深入分析了恶搞行为的成因，发现其背后可能源于特定的社会环境和心理因素，而非个体的性格缺陷。这一发现挑战了传统对恶搞者的刻板印象，提示我们在理解网络行为时应考虑更复杂的社会心理背景。

在实验中，研究者们观察了参与者在不同社交环境下的行为表现，发现那些在压力较大或社交互动不良的环境中，恶搞行为的发生率显著增加。这表明，恶搞行为可能与个体所处的社会情境密切相关，而不是单纯由个体的性格特征决定。此外，研究还发现，某些心理因素，如寻求关注、获得社交认同等，可能驱动普通人在特定情况下选择恶搞行为。

通过对这些现象的分析，研究团队强调了理解网络恶搞行为的复杂性，认为应从社会心理学的角度出发，综合考虑环境、情境和个体心理等多重因素。这一研究不仅为我们提供了对网络恶搞行为的新视角，也为改善网络社交环境、减少恶搞行为提供了理论依据。总之，本文的研究结果表明，网络恶搞并非简单的个体缺陷，而是社会和心理因素交织的产物，呼吁我们在面对网络行为时，采取更加全面和深入的理解。
items.l3_translation:
像这样的评论，在关于女性如何看待自己的CNN文章中被发现，今天在互联网上普遍存在，无论是在Facebook、Reddit还是新闻网站上。这种行为可以从粗口和辱骂到人身攻击、性骚扰或仇恨言论不等。

几年前的一项皮尤互联网调查发现，四分之一的在线用户曾遭受过网络骚扰，更多的人目睹过这种行为。网络喷子现象已经变得如此猖獗，以至于一些网站甚至不得不完全删除评论。

许多人认为，网络喷子是少数声音很大的反社会个体。这种看法不仅在媒体中得到了强化，也在过去关于网络喷子的研究中得到了支持，这些研究集中于采访这些个体。一些研究甚至表明，网络喷子具有某些倾向性的人格和生物特征，例如施虐倾向和寻求过度刺激的倾向。

但如果并非所有的网络喷子都是天生的呢？如果他们和你我一样是普通人呢？在我们的研究中，我们发现，在特定情况下，普通人可以被影响去网络喷其他人。通过分析在CNN.com上发表的1600万条评论并进行在线控制实验，我们确定了两个关键因素，这些因素可以导致普通人变成网络喷子。

我们通过一个在线众包平台招募了667名参与者，并要求他们首先参加一个测验，然后阅读一篇文章并参与讨论。每位参与者看到的都是同一篇文章，但有些人看到的是以网络喷子评论开头的讨论，而其他人则看到的是中立评论。在这里，网络喷子的定义是基于标准社区指南——例如，辱骂、粗口、种族主义或骚扰。之前的测验也有所不同，有的比较简单，有的比较困难。

我们对CNN.com上评论的分析帮助验证并扩展了这些实验观察。

似乎影响网络喷子的第一个因素是一个人的情绪。在我们的实验中，处于负面情绪中的人更有可能开始网络喷子。我们还发现，网络喷子的行为随着一天中的时间和一周中的天数而波动，与自然的人类情绪模式同步。网络喷子在深夜最为频繁，而在早晨最少。网络喷子的行为在周一达到高峰，正值工作周的开始。

此外，我们发现，负面情绪可以在引发这些情绪的事件之后持续存在。假设一个人参与了一个讨论，而其他人写了网络喷子的评论。如果这个人随后参与一个无关的讨论，他们在那个讨论中也更有可能进行网络喷子。

第二个因素是讨论的上下文。如果一个讨论以“网络喷子评论”开始，那么后续其他参与者进行网络喷子的可能性是没有以网络喷子评论开始的讨论的两倍。

事实上，这些网络喷子评论可以累积。在一个讨论中，网络喷子评论越多，未来参与者也越可能进行网络喷子。总的来说，这些结果显示，讨论中的初始评论为后续的网络喷子行为设定了强烈而持久的先例。

我们想知道，利用这两个因素，我们是否可以预测网络喷子何时会发生。通过使用机器学习算法，我们能够预测一个人是否会进行网络喷子的准确率约为80%。

有趣的是，情绪和讨论上下文共同成为网络喷子的更强指示因素，而不是识别特定个体作为网络喷子。换句话说，网络喷子的原因更多地来自于个人的环境，而不是任何固有特征。

由于网络喷子是情境性的，普通人可以受到影响而进行网络喷子，因此这种行为可能会在人与人之间传播。在一个讨论中，一个网络喷子评论——也许是由一个早上心情不佳的人写的——可能导致其他参与者的情绪变差，甚至在其他地方产生更多的网络喷子评论。随着这种负面行为的持续传播，如果不加以控制，网络喷子可能最终成为社区中的常态。

尽管这些结果令人警醒，但这项研究有几种方法可以帮助我们创造更好的公共讨论在线空间。

通过理解导致网络喷子的因素，我们现在可以更好地预测网络喷子何时可能发生。这可以让我们提前识别潜在的争议讨论，并提前警告版主，版主可以在这些激烈的情况下进行干预。

机器学习算法也可以比任何人更快地筛选数百万条帖子。通过训练计算机识别网络喷子行为，我们可以更快速地识别和过滤不良内容。

社会干预也可以减少网络喷子。如果我们允许人们撤回最近发布的评论，那么我们可能能够减少在情绪激动时发布的后悔。通过优先考虑建设性评论来改变讨论的上下文，可以增强对文明的感知。即使只是将关于社区规则的帖子置顶在讨论页面上，也会有所帮助，正如最近在Reddit上进行的一项实验所示。

尽管如此，仍有很多工作要做以解决网络喷子问题。理解有组织的网络喷子的角色可以限制某些类型的不良行为。

网络喷子的严重程度也可能不同，从咒骂到针对性的欺凌，这需要不同的应对措施。

区分网络喷子评论的影响与作者的意图也很重要：这个网络喷子是故意想伤害他人，还是只是想表达不同的观点？这可以帮助将不良个体与那些只是需要帮助表达自己想法的人区分开来。

当在线讨论崩溃时，不仅仅是反社会者应该受到指责。我们也有责任。许多“网络喷子”只是和我们一样正在经历糟糕的一天。理解我们对激励和压抑的责任是至关重要的。

items.title: People with disability are dying from cancers we can actually prevent, our study shows
items.body: People with disability are more likely to die from cancer than the overall population. Here’s how we can shift this striking inequity.
items.authors: Yi Yang
items.attribution_basis: The Conversation 作者页 /profiles/yi-yang-2270524（名+姓双命中）
items.title_zh: 残疾人因可预防癌症而死亡的现象亟需关注
items.summary_zh: 研究表明，残疾人群体死于癌症的风险高于整体人口。这一现象揭示了医疗资源和预防措施在不同人群中的不平等分配。通过改善医疗服务的可及性、加强健康教育以及提供针对性的预防措施，我们可以有效降低残疾人群体的癌症死亡率。研究强调，采取行动以消除这一显著的不平等现象是当务之急。
items.l1_lead: 残疾人群体因可预防癌症而死亡的风险高于整体人口，亟需改善医疗资源分配和预防措施以降低其癌症死亡率。
items.l2_summary: 残疾人因可预防癌症而死亡的现象亟需引起社会的广泛关注。研究表明，残疾人群体死于癌症的风险显著高于整体人口，这一现象反映出医疗资源和预防措施在不同人群中的不平等分配。残疾人由于身体条件的限制，往往面临更大的健康风险，尤其是在癌症的早期筛查和治疗方面，缺乏必要的医疗支持和信息获取渠道。因此，改善医疗服务的可及性、加强健康教育以及提供针对性的预防措施显得尤为重要。通过这些措施，我们可以有效降低残疾人群体的癌症死亡率，帮助他们获得与其他人群同等的健康保障。研究强调，采取行动以消除这一显著的不平等现象是当务之急，只有通过系统性的改变，才能确保每一个人都能享有平等的医疗服务和健康机会。
items.l3_translation:
残疾人士正在错过可能帮助早期发现癌症的筛查项目，而在确诊后，他们的生存几率较低，我们的研究显示。

总体而言，这意味着残疾人士死于癌症的可能性高于非残疾人士。

我们汇集了证据，显示当前癌症控制方法中存在显著的不平等。

但有办法改善许多非残疾人士常规使用的筛查项目和癌症服务的获取。

我们回顾了来自全球73项研究的证据。这些研究比较了残疾人士与非残疾人士的癌症结果。

让我们从癌症筛查开始，这是预防癌症死亡的一种方式。筛查可以发现癌症的早期迹象，或者如果及时发现，可以防止其发展成问题。早期发现通常意味着更多的治疗选择和更高的良好结果几率。

然而，我们的回顾发现，残疾人士在全球范围内错过了这些拯救生命的筛查项目，包括乳腺癌、宫颈癌和肠癌的筛查。

事实上，我们回顾中的一些研究显示，这些癌症在残疾人士中更可能在晚期被诊断。

一旦确诊，残疾人士仍处于不利地位。我们发现他们的生存率低于非残疾癌症患者。

这可能是由于诊断延迟和治疗不可及，我们需要进一步研究以确认。但我们确实有一些研究提供了相关证据。

一项关于智力残疾人士癌症死亡的英国研究发现，超过三分之一的癌症是在他们去急诊科后被诊断的。研究中几乎一半的癌症在确诊时已经处于晚期。

另一项全球证据的回顾发现，残疾癌症患者接受的癌症护理质量较差。这包括治疗延迟、治疗不足或接受过于侵入性的治疗。残疾人士在住院服务和止痛药方面的获取也较少。

从诊断到治疗，全球证据显示，残疾人士被排除在许多非残疾人士常规获取和受益的健康服务之外。

在澳大利亚情况也没有不同，这正在夺去生命。

在之前的研究中，我们发现癌症是澳大利亚残疾人士早逝的主要原因。它是导致残疾人士比非残疾人士多出约20%额外死亡的原因。

我们显然需要做更多工作来改善残疾人士的医疗保健。但我们也需要在其他领域采取行动，以解决潜在问题。

残疾人士比澳大利亚其他人口更可能生活在贫困和不利的环境中，这可能使他们面临更高的癌症风险。

导致癌症的许多因素——例如吸烟、无法负担的健康食品和高水平饮酒——对包括残疾人士在内的弱势群体产生不成比例的影响。

许多残疾人士还伴有其他健康状况，这可能导致对常规问题的关注不足。这可能导致癌症筛查和常规护理变得不那么优先。

提供服务的建筑物和医疗诊断设备并不总是对残疾人士可及。

健康系统本身也可能是不可及的，几乎没有支持帮助残疾人士获取服务。例如，导航癌症护理可能令人不知所措，尤其是对于需要日常活动、交通或沟通支持的人。

残疾人士，尤其是智力残疾人士，需要额外的时间和支持，以便对筛查、治疗或程序给予知情同意——这些资源和时间在公共卫生系统中尤其紧张。

残疾人士在医疗保健中也可能经历直接和间接的歧视，这导致较差的结果。这包括对残疾人士及其照顾者的歧视性态度，以及基于患者的残疾做出假设。

为了使癌症控制具有包容性并为残疾人士服务，我们需要关注以下几个方面：

预防——公共卫生干预措施，例如戒烟或健康生活方式项目，需要与残疾人士共同设计并量身定制。

早期发现——国家筛查项目必须制定策略并采取积极措施以包括残疾人士。诊所需要在物理上可及，信息需要以多种可获取的格式提供，并且需要分配额外的时间以获得真正的知情同意。

确保残疾人士有发言权——癌症护理需要根据个人的需求量身定制，因为每个人的需求都不同。我们需要支持并让残疾人士参与关于其护理的对话，以便他们能够做出知情决定。这意味着以适合他们的方式提供信息，并留出时间以理解和提问。

培训医疗专业人员理解和响应残疾人士的需求，并做出必要的调整以提供最佳的癌症护理，特别是对于智力残疾人士。

研究员，社会流行病学，墨尔本残疾研究所，墨尔本大学人口与全球健康学院

items.title: NDIS reforms aim to make the scheme fairer. But we’ve found the groups struggling to gain access
items.body: Factors like age, gender and where you live can make it more likely an applicant will be rejected.
items.authors: Yi Yang
items.attribution_basis: The Conversation 作者页 /profiles/yi-yang-2270524（名+姓双命中）
items.title_zh: NDIS改革旨在提高公平性，但仍有群体难以获得支持
items.summary_zh: 本文评述了澳大利亚国家残疾保险计划（NDIS）的改革，旨在提升该计划的公平性。然而，研究发现，申请者的年龄、性别和居住地等因素可能导致其被拒绝的可能性增加。这表明，尽管改革措施的实施，仍有特定群体在获取NDIS支持方面面临挑战，亟需进一步的关注和改进。
items.l1_lead: 尽管NDIS改革旨在提高公平性，但年龄、性别和居住地等因素仍导致特定群体难以获得支持，需进一步改进。
items.l2_summary: 澳大利亚国家残疾保险计划（NDIS）近年来进行了一系列改革，旨在提升该计划的公平性，以确保更多残疾人士能够获得必要的支持。然而，研究表明，尽管这些改革措施已实施，仍有一些特定群体在申请NDIS支持时面临显著挑战。具体而言，申请者的年龄、性别和居住地等因素被发现与其获得支持的可能性密切相关。例如，某些年龄段的申请者可能更容易被拒绝，而性别和地理位置的差异也可能导致不同群体在申请过程中遭遇不平等待遇。这些发现表明，NDIS在实现公平性方面仍存在不足，尤其是在对特定群体的支持上。为了真正实现公平，政策制定者需要对这些影响因素进行深入分析，并采取针对性的措施，以确保所有残疾人士都能平等地获得所需的支持和服务。因此，尽管NDIS改革的初衷是为了提升公平性，但在实际操作中，仍需关注和改善那些在申请过程中遭遇困难的群体，以实现更全面的公平和包容。
items.l3_translation:
当国家残疾保险计划（NDIS）在2013年成立时，其主要目标之一是使残疾服务和支持系统更加公平。

然而，我们的新研究显示，仍然存在显著的不平等，一些群体发现被认定为符合条件并获得资金计划的难度远大于其他群体。

最近的NDIS改革部分旨在解决不平等问题，并管理成本。

那么，我们可以做些什么来确保这些改革不会进一步加深现有的不平等呢？以下是我们的发现。

要从NDIS获得资金，参与者需要证明他们的资格。

我们想探讨关于资格的决定是否导致了谁能够获得和使用NDIS资金的不平等。

我们的研究考察了485,676名年龄在七岁或以上的个人在2016年至2022年间提交的NDIS申请，以查看他们是否被认定为符合条件。

然后，我们比较了不同群体之间的资格率差异，考虑了以下因素：

我们发现某些群体被拒绝进入该计划的可能性高于其他群体：女性和女孩、55岁及以上的人，以及生活在贫困地区的人。

在这些群体中，资格率也有所不同。

例如，智力残疾、自闭症以及脑损伤或中风的人被认定为符合条件的可能性很高，无论他们的年龄、性别或社会经济劣势如何（每1,000名申请者中有900人或更多被接受）。

然而，身体残疾和心理社会残疾（可能由心理健康问题引起的残疾，如双相情感障碍或精神分裂症）的人被拒绝的可能性显著更高。

这一现象在各个群体中都存在，但在女性和女孩中尤为明显。

我们比较了每1,000份女性和女孩的申请与男性和男孩的申请之间的资格率。

在身体残疾者中，女性和女孩被拒绝的数量比男性和男孩多出145人。

在心理社会残疾者中，每1,000份女性的申请中，有83份被认定为不符合条件，相比之下，男性的申请则没有。

年龄也是一个因素。年长的身体残疾澳大利亚人每1,000份申请的批准数量比55岁以下的身体残疾者少235个。

在试图证明资格的人群中，不平等现象更加明显。

一旦被接受进入NDIS，我们的研究发现，女性和女孩以及生活在贫困地区的人获得的资金与男性和男孩以及生活在富裕地区的人相似。

这个预算是基于参与者在日常生活中想要实现的目标以及与他们的残疾相关的支持需求。

然而，一旦人们获得并使用计划，我们就会看到这些人能够支出的金额存在一些差异。这与服务在某个地区的可用性或是否提供文化安全的支持等因素有关。

我们发现，心理社会残疾的女性支出的金额超过了预算相似的男性。

这一结果可能反映出，NDIS中心理社会残疾的女性比男性有更高的支持需求。

也可能是女性更难以进入该计划，因此那些被认定为符合条件的女性残疾程度比男性更为严重。

但我们需要更多的研究来进一步探讨这一问题。

在NDIS的早期阶段，为了帮助加快申请处理，国家残疾保险机构（负责运营NDIS）指定了一份与残疾密切相关的诊断清单。

被称为A类条件，拥有这些诊断的人自动符合NDIS的资格。

与A类诊断相关的残疾可能包括2级或3级自闭症（需要大量或非常大量的支持）和智力残疾。

然而，一些可能具有永久性和显著残疾的人，可能有不在A类清单上的诊断，例如唐氏综合症和运动神经元病。他们必须提供更广泛的证据来证明残疾的影响，以便符合资格。

如果他们面临其他挑战——例如社会经济劣势——那么收集这些证据可能会更加困难。例如，他们可能无法负担能够帮助支持其申请的私人医疗保健。

这可能解释了为什么没有A类诊断的人更不可能证明他们符合该计划的资格。

根据对NDIS的独立审查的建议，国家残疾保险机构目前正在改变其资格评估的方式。

建议的其中一项变化是完全取消A类分类。

相反，该机构将使用一套功能评估工具。这些工具仍在设计过程中，但它们是评估一个人执行日常任务能力和识别他们所需支持水平的一种方式。

这种方法旨在更客观和公平地评估某人受到残疾影响的程度。

然而，这些工具长期以来受到批评。这些批评包括对它们对少数群体（如具有文化或语言多样性背景的人、LGBTQIA+人群和原住民申请者）是否安全的担忧。

我们的新研究展示了某些不平等是如何以及为何产生的。我们应该将这种理解放在任何对NDIS的变更的核心位置。

最重要的是，我们应该确保改革与广泛的不同群体共同设计，以确保我们不会延续旧的不平等或引入新的不平等。

items.title: Australians with disability are 4 times more likely to die early – often not due to their disability
items.body: People with disability die of conditions such as cancer, heart disease and diabetes at a much higher rate than the rest of the population.
items.authors: Yi Yang
items.attribution_basis: The Conversation 作者页 /profiles/yi-yang-2270524（名+姓双命中）
items.title_zh: 残疾澳大利人早逝风险是普通人四倍
items.summary_zh: 研究显示，残疾人士因癌症、心脏病和糖尿病等疾病的死亡率远高于普通人群。尽管残疾可能影响健康状况，但早逝的主要原因往往并非直接由残疾引起。这一现象揭示了残疾人士在医疗和健康管理方面面临的重大挑战，强调了需要改善对残疾人士的健康服务和支持，以降低他们的早逝风险。
items.l1_lead: 残疾澳大利人因疾病早逝风险是普通人的四倍，凸显了改善其医疗和健康管理服务的紧迫性。
items.l2_summary:
一项研究显示，残疾澳大利人的早逝风险是普通人群的四倍，表明残疾人士在健康方面面临着严峻的挑战。研究发现，残疾人士因癌症、心脏病和糖尿病等疾病的死亡率显著高于没有残疾的个体。这一现象虽然与残疾本身的健康状况有关，但早逝的主要原因往往并非直接由残疾引起。这提示我们，残疾人士在医疗和健康管理方面遭遇的障碍可能更为复杂，涉及到社会、经济和环境等多方面的因素。

研究强调，残疾人士在获取医疗服务和健康支持时，常常面临诸多困难，这可能导致他们的健康状况进一步恶化，进而增加早逝的风险。因此，改善对残疾人士的健康服务和支持显得尤为重要。通过提供更为全面和有效的医疗资源，能够帮助降低残疾人士的早逝风险，提升他们的生活质量。

总的来说，这项研究不仅揭示了残疾人士在健康管理中所面临的重大挑战，也呼吁社会各界关注并改善残疾人士的健康服务，以实现更公平的医疗保障。
items.l3_translation:
当Finlay Browne在仅16岁时去世时，他的死亡证明上列出了“唐氏综合症”作为死亡原因。

但芬利并不是死于唐氏综合症。今年早些时候，一名法医发现这名青少年因肠梗阻并发症而死，并指出他所在地方医院提供的“护理和治疗的充分性问题”。

自芬利去世以来，他的家人多次发声，呼吁改善智力残疾人士的医疗保健。

但遗憾的是，芬利并不是孤单的。我们在《柳叶刀公共卫生》上发表的新研究显示，残疾人士早逝的可能性是非残疾人士的四倍左右。

我们查看了2011年至2020年间超过1500万名0至74岁澳大利亚人的人口普查数据，并分析了在此期间去世的人的死亡证明信息（约463,000人）。

我们发现，残疾人士因癌症、心脏病、慢性肺病和糖尿病等疾病的死亡率远高于其他人群。

残疾男性的死亡率几乎是非残疾男性的四倍。同时，残疾女性的死亡率几乎是她们非残疾同龄人的五倍。

虽然我们的研究利用了大型数据集并使用了复杂的统计技术，但我们意识到图表上的点代表了许多像芬利一样的过早和可预防的死亡。

导致许多残疾澳大利亚人早逝的疾病通常在生活在贫困环境中的人群中更为常见。我们知道，贫困、低质量住房和被排除在医疗系统之外会导致早逝。这些情况在残疾人士中比整体人群更为普遍。

残疾人士在获取良好医疗保健时面临与许多其他澳大利亚人相同的问题，例如可用性不足、成本上升和等待时间过长。但他们还面临额外的挑战。例如：

健康服务所在的建筑并不总是对残疾人士可及。

残疾人士有时会遭遇包括全科医生、护士和医院工作人员在内的医疗人员的歧视。

残疾人士通常会因相同的健康状况看多个健康专业人员，并报告治疗他们的健康专业人员之间缺乏沟通。

不幸的是，我们研究的结果并不令人惊讶。残疾人士、家庭和倡导组织多年来一直在谈论残疾人士的健康结果不佳，以及那些通过适当行动本可以预防的早逝。

最近的关于残疾人士暴力、虐待、忽视和剥削的皇家委员会直接听取了残疾人士关于贫困、住房不良和医疗系统歧视对健康和福祉影响的意见。

我们的研究是澳大利亚首个此类规模的研究，这一点很重要。

历史上，了解死亡原因的模式为我们的公共卫生优先事项提供了信息。但到目前为止，残疾人士的死亡原因模式在很大程度上没有被优先考虑、收集或分析。由于数据不足，公共卫生工作系统性地忽视了残疾人士。

然而，残疾人士的健康结果不佳并不是不可避免的。

我们需要在澳大利亚的城市、地区和乡村看到协调一致的行动，以防止更多不必要的死亡。作为一个国家，我们需要解决许多残疾人士生活的条件——从贫困和缺乏负担得起的、可及的住房开始。

我们还需要使医疗保健对残疾人士更可及和负担得起。

但是，如果我们不正面面对医疗保健中的歧视，这些都将不够。这将涉及在医疗保健的各个层面进行政策、流程和系统的变更，以适应残疾人士的需求。

我们还需要考虑我们的普遍疾病预防策略，部分策略取得了巨大的成功，是否覆盖到残疾人士。例如，残疾人士是否能够以与其他人相同的方式获得常规筛查？还是他们被排除在外？

最终，我们需要揭穿“健康不佳是残疾的一部分”这一神话。不可避免的是，除非我们采取行动，并将残疾人士的健康和福祉作为国家优先事项，否则残疾澳大利亚人将继续早逝。

items.title: Scalable photonic quantum technologies.
items.body: Photonic quantum technologies are now progressing from demonstrations of fundamental phenomena to systems of sufficient scale and quality to enable practical applications with quantum advantage in communications, computation and metrology. Here we review recent advances in quantum optics that have led to the emergence of such scalable quantum technologies, and outline the road ahead to more general applications with greater potential impact. We first focus on the components that support various photonic quantum applications, including quantum light sources, linear-optical networks and detectors. We go on to discuss recent experimental demonstrations of quantum communication, quantum computation and simulation, and quantum metrology using photons. Finally, an overview is provided on the manner in which photons fit within both the opportunities and challenges of implementing space-to-ground quantum internet, universal quantum computing and quantum precision measurement.
items.authors: Wang H, Ralph TC, Renema JJ, Lu CY, Pan JW.
items.title_zh: 可扩展的光子量子技术进展
items.summary_zh: 光子量子技术正从基础现象的演示向足够规模和质量的系统发展，以实现通信、计算和计量中的量子优势。本文回顾了量子光学的最新进展，这些进展促成了可扩展量子技术的出现，并概述了未来更广泛应用的前景。我们首先关注支持各种光子量子应用的组件，包括量子光源、线性光学网络和探测器。接着讨论了利用光子进行的量子通信、量子计算与模拟以及量子计量的最新实验演示。最后，概述了光子在实现地面与太空量子互联网、通用量子计算和量子精密测量中的机遇与挑战。
items.l1_lead: 光子量子技术正向可扩展系统发展，推动量子通信、计算和计量的应用，展现出广阔的未来前景。
items.l2_summary:
光子量子技术正逐步从基础现象的演示向具备足够规模和质量的系统发展，以实现量子通信、量子计算和量子计量中的量子优势。近年来，量子光学领域取得了显著进展，这些进展为可扩展量子技术的实现奠定了基础。本文回顾了支持各种光子量子应用的关键组件，包括量子光源（quantum light sources）、线性光学网络（linear optical networks）和探测器（detectors），这些组件的不断优化和创新为量子技术的应用提供了重要支撑。

在量子通信方面，利用光子进行的实验演示显示出其在信息传输中的潜力，尤其是在安全性和效率方面。量子计算与模拟的研究同样取得了重要进展，通过光子实现的量子计算模型展现了其在处理复杂计算任务中的优势。此外，量子计量的实验也表明，光子技术能够在精密测量中提供更高的准确性和灵敏度。

展望未来，光子在实现地面与太空量子互联网、通用量子计算和量子精密测量方面蕴含着巨大的机遇。然而，这些应用的实现也面临着诸多挑战，包括技术的可扩展性、系统的稳定性以及环境噪声的影响等。因此，尽管光子量子技术的发展前景广阔，但仍需在技术和理论层面进行深入研究，以克服当前的障碍，实现更广泛的应用。总的来说，光子量子技术的进步为未来量子信息科学的发展提供了新的动力和方向。

items.title: Quantum information meets high-energy physics: input to the update of the European strategy for particle physics.
items.body: Some of the most astonishing and prominent properties of Quantum Mechanics, such as entanglement and Bell nonlocality, have only been studied extensively in dedicated low-energy laboratory setups. The feasibility of these studies in the high-energy regime explored by particle colliders was only recently shown and has gathered the attention of the scientific community. For the range of particles and fundamental interactions involved, particle colliders provide a novel environment where quantum information theory can be probed, with energies exceeding by about 12 orders of magnitude those employed in dedicated laboratory setups. Furthermore, collider detectors have inherent advantages in performing certain quantum information measurements and allow for the reconstruction of the state of the system under consideration via quantum state tomography. Here, we elaborate on the potential, challenges, and goals of this innovative and rapidly evolving line of research and discuss its expected impact on both quantum information theory and high-energy physics.
items.authors: Afik Y, Fabbri F, Low M, Marzola L, Aguilar-Saavedra JA, Altakach MM, Asbah NA, Bai Y, Banks H, Barr AJ, Bernal A, Browder TE, Caban P, Casas JA, Cheng K, Déliot F, Demina R, Di Domenico A, Eckstein M, Fabbrichesi M, Fuk
