items.title: Is Immortality Possible? - Nautilus | Science Connected
items.body:
原话：“I don’t think it’s an impossibility, but it’s incredibly difficult.” / “An organism doesn’t want cells capable of indefinite reproduction, because that’s a cancer risk. You can think of senescence as evolution’s way of preventing cancer.” / “It’s just fantasies at this point, and a distraction from our real problems.”
论点：延长人类寿命的尝试是极其困难的，且可能带来癌症风险。
论据：大约2000个主控基因协调早期胚胎发育，调节这些基因以实现长寿的能力远超我们目前的能力。
items.authors: Venki Ramakrishnan
items.attribution_basis: Google News 全名命中 + LLM 同一人核验（Nautilus | Science Connected） + 论点方向独立复核
quotes: I don’t think it’s an impossibility, but it’s incredibly difficult.
An organism doesn’t want cells capable of indefinite reproduction, because that’s a cancer risk. You can think of senescence as evolution’s way of preventing cancer.
It’s just fantasies at this point, and a distraction from our real problems.
items.topic_zh: 人类寿命与抗衰老研究的挑战
items.claim_zh: 延长人类寿命的尝试是极其困难的，且可能带来癌症风险。
items.evidence_zh: 大约2000个主控基因协调早期胚胎发育，调节这些基因以实现长寿的能力远超我们目前的能力。
items.article_body:
Menu Subscribe Log In Astronomy Environment Evolution History Philosophy Psychology Zoology Search Search Astronomy Environment Evolution History Philosophy Psychology Zoology FAQ Contact Awards and Press Privacy Policy Terms of Service RSS Jobs Newsletter Ethics Policy Log In Subscribe Nautilus Facebook Nautilus X (formerly Twitter) Nautilus TikTok Nautilus YouTube Nautilus Bluesky Nautilus Instagram Advertisement Evolution Is Immortality Possible? Nature has answered the same way for 3.5 billion years
Add Nautilus to Google 2 Comments There are all these people who say that death is natural, it’s just part of life, and I think that nothing can be further from the truth,” Peter Thiel told Business Insider in 2012. The venture capitalist has spent years backing efforts to slow or defeat aging, and his provocation captures the confidence of a wider Silicon Valley project: Given enough money and biological engineering, death may become just another technical problem to solve.
Nature, it seems, remains wholly uninspired by Silicon Valley capital. Scientific insight into 3.5 billion years of evolution suggests that death isn’t a glitch—it’s working as intended. That does not mean every organism carries a simple genetic suicide switch, or that every death is adaptive. It simply means that natural selection favors reproductive success over immortality. It also explains aging as the ultimate compromise for a body balancing the competing energetic requirements of development, reproduction, and repair.
“There is a cost to living, a cost to doing everything” Nick Lane, a biochemist at University College London, told Philip Ball in an interview with Nautilus . Lane examines life through the lens of energetics. He studies how much energy is required for life’s various processes, and how organisms go about acquiring and spending it.
“If we are living our lives at a very fast rate, we tend to, in effect, wear out sooner,” Lane said. Living is strenuous work. Growth, mating, pregnancy, parental care, and immune defense all consume energy and take a physical toll. Because maintenance and repair are themselves energetically costly, they must be traded off against these processes.
Across the animal kingdom, species have evolved different ways of allocating energy throughout their lives, mostly according to their size and exposure to external hazards. One consequence of this is that animals have vastly different natural lifespans.
Consider the mouse and the elephant. In the wild, a field mouse can live up to two years, whereas an elephant can live to 70. But mice are small and die easily, from predators or harsh weather. In such easy prey, natural selection is highly skewed toward early reproduction. An expensive body maintenance program for a distant (and highly unlikely) old age makes no sense. For an elephant, which matures slowly and faces fewer predators, evolution has selected for a durable body and a longer lifespan.
Overall, smaller species live fast lives, reproduce early, and die young. “There is a very strong relationship between metabolic rate, the rate at which we’re taking in oxygen and burning up food, and lifespan,” Lane said. This may help explain, at least partially, why caloric restriction can double or treble the lifespan of very simple organisms, like worms or fruit flies. Without calories, reproduction is unlikely and organisms enter a phase of “battening down the hatches and waiting out the bad times,” Lane said. But humans, of course, are far more complex. Our bodies are finely tuned to run at a metabolic rate held within narrow limits. Simply restricting calories in our diet would lead our bodies to burn up protein in muscle and other tissues.
In fact, humans are unusually long-lived for primates of our size. “Given our body mass, we live about twice as long [as we should for our size],” Venki Ramakrishnan, the Nobel Prize-winning structural biologist and author of Why We Die , told me. Improvements in nutrition, sanitation, and medicine have doubled the average human lifespan over the past 150 years, but our longevity has deeper roots. Michelangelo, Ramakrishnan noted, lived to nearly 90 in the 16th century, and some researchers believe human lifespans began lengthening as far back as 40,000 years ago. The drivers for the change remain unclear, Ramakrishnan said. A leading hypothesis links a sudden shift in human lifespan to the evolutionary perks of having grandparents in hunter-gatherer communities. Older adults helped raise children while parents were busy providing food. In times of crises, their accumulated knowledge of the environment gave their tribe a decisive edge in survival.
Given that modern humans have escaped many of the hazards that once made longevity a poor evolutionary investment, and that leaps in lifespan are possible, it makes sense to wonder if perhaps the billionaires have a case. Or, as Ramakrishnan put it, “The real question is, we have mechanisms for repairing damage, so why don’t we just keep repairing our body and live forever?”
The answer cuts to the heart of aging research.
Even in the absence of multiple stressors—we live comfortable lives indoors sheltered from environmental extremes and carry a significantly lower pathogen load than our ancestors—our bodies have evolved to keep the time. In 2022, Steve Horvath, a professor at the University of California, Los Angeles and a leading figure in anti-aging research, uncovered the existence of a molecular clock , a universal, internal mechanism that marks the age of mammalian cells and tissues. It reveals that aging is neither entirely random nor simply the accumulation of visible wear.
Throughout a cell’s life, patterns of chemical tags on DNA (called epigenetic markers) accumulate. Horvath developed a formula that reliably deciphers the pattern to predict the age of cells and tissues. This pattern is the “biological” age of the cell, which closely aligns with, but doesn’t always precisely map, chronological age. Its accuracy (for humans, it is exact to plus or minus 3.6 years) implies that aging is a carefully maintained biological process, rather than a haphazard set of events. We speed up the clock with things like smoking and excessive alcohol consumption.
Some scientists interpreted Horvath’s discovery—that all tissues count time—as indication that we are programmed to die, our cells marching inexorably toward death. But Horvath’s own interpretation swerves clear of such determinism and focuses instead on what the clock achieves in our early years.
We don’t think of babies as aging, but that is when the aging program is most active. Embryonic cells (which start off identical) need to differentiate quickly and in perfect synchrony into tissues, building organs and a body that continues to mature into adulthood. An internal metronome serves the essential function of orchestrating the elaborate process. But after adulthood, the program continues to run, and runs us all the way to the ground. “Evolution did not select a program that makes us die,” Horvath said. Instead, “Mother Nature never selected against it.”
As Ramakrishnan told me, “Death is an unintended consequence of aging.” And aging is an unintended consequence of development. Research shows that once development is complete (once we reach reproductive age), some of the genetic machinery that enabled it can keep running, or become reactivated as its regulation deteriorates, with increasingly harmful effects. In old mice, for example , the gene Hoxa9 , which is essential to a developing embryo, switched back on in muscle stem cells, activating obsolete developmental pathways that hindered muscle repair.
One of the hallmarks of aging is cellular senescence. It is a state in which damaged or stressed cells permanently stop dividing yet resist dying, accumulating in tissues over time. Though senescence initially protects against cancer by halting the growth of compromised cells, senescent cells secrete inflammatory molecules that harm surrounding tissue and drive many features of aging.
The runaway developmental programs of old age stem from the same evolutionary trade-off that links metabolism to lifespans. Selection prioritizes early biological performance (the period before reproduction happens) over late-life durability. A gene that promotes development or improves fertility and survival at 20 can be favored even if it raises the risk of degeneration at 70. A defect expressed only at 90 will encounter limited evolutionary pressure. Death is a compounding of the problem across a genome composed of genes all acting under the same selection. It is the final bill for evolution’s early favors.
All of this makes anti-aging innovations extremely challenging . Roughly 2,000 master control genes orchestrate early embryonic development, supported by another 5,000 to 10,000 organ-building genes. Re-tuning them for longevity without wreaking havoc is well beyond our current capabilities. “I don’t think it’s an impossibility, but it’s incredibly difficult,” Ramakrishnan told me.
The most immediate threat of getting this balance wrong is cancer. That’s because the signaling pathways that encourage cells to divide and repair tissues in early life are the exact same pathways that tumors hijack to proliferate unchecked. Override those aging pathways, and you remove the guards keeping malignancy at bay.
Researchers have already encountered this trade-off in one of the best-studied longevity pathways, which involves growth hormone (GH) and insulin-like growth factor 1 (IGF-1). Because IGF-1 promotes cell growth, muscle maintenance, and tissue repair, boosting its activity once seemed a plausible anti-aging strategy.
Read more: “ Physics Makes Aging Inevitable, Not Biology ”
But the same signals that encourage healthy cells to regenerate can also encourage precancerous cells to survive and multiply. Animal studies consistently show that reducing GH and IGF-1 signaling extends lifespan while lowering cancer incidence, whereas chronically elevated IGF-1 activity is associated with an increased risk of several cancers. The pathway that helps build and maintain the body in youth can become a liability when kept active into old age.
This compromise should not be entirely surprising. Adult stem cells possess an unusual capacity for long-term self-renewal, while cancer cells achieve essentially limitless proliferation by escaping the body’s normal controls. Efforts to make ordinary cells more regenerative inevitably edge them toward the biology of tumors. “An organism doesn’t want cells capable of indefinite reproduction,” Ramakrishnan said, “because that’s a cancer risk. You can think of senescence as evolution’s way of preventing cancer.”
The pattern is becoming uncannily familiar throughout aging biology: Molecules and pathways once cast as villains often turn out to have essential functions. For decades, scientists believed that aging was largely driven by the accumulation of damage from reactive oxygen molecules, or free radicals, produced by mitochondria. The theory was so influential that antioxidant supplements were widely promoted to slow aging. But decades of research have failed to support that idea.
Large clinical studies found little evidence that high-dose antioxidant supplements extend life or prevent age-related disease, and some have even linked them to worse outcomes. Rather than being merely destructive, Lane explained, free radicals act as vital cellular signals. “They are behaving a little bit like the smoke detector,” he said. When cells detect those signals, they activate genetic programs that repair damage, strengthen stress resistance, and help the cell survive. Blunting that signal indiscriminately is counterproductive. “The trouble with antioxidants is they’re in effect disabling the smoke detector,” Lane said.
A similar paradox occurs with anti-aging therapies that target the inflammatory response. Inflammation is essential
items.title_zh: 不朽是否可能？科学家的观点探讨
items.summary_zh: 本文探讨了延长人类寿命的可能性及其面临的挑战。科学家指出，尽管不朽并非绝对不可能，但实现这一目标极其困难，且可能带来癌症风险。生物体并不希望细胞具备无限繁殖的能力，因为这会增加癌症的风险。衰老（senescence）可以被视为进化防止癌症的一种方式。此外，约2000个主控基因协调早期胚胎发育，而调节这些基因以实现长寿的能力远超我们目前的技术水平。因此，延长寿命的尝试在现阶段仍然是一个充满幻想的领域，可能会分散我们对现实问题的关注。

items.body:

He felt he couldn’t go on.” / “at the heart of all this was a man who was diagnosed with autism and language differences…he needed support every step of the way… after the allegations of plagiarism, [the] media didn’t leave him alone.”

items.topic_zh: 对Jason Arday的同情与理解
items.claim_zh: Jason Arday在面对媒体的持续压力和职业生涯的丧失时，感到无法承受，缺乏必要的支持。
items.evidence_zh: 他被持续的审视和嘲笑所困扰，失去了职业和声誉。
items.article_body:
Coffee House Melanie McDonagh The tragedy of Jason Arday Saturday, August 15, 2026, 10:30 AM Jason Arday (Credit: BBC) Text settings Text size Small Medium Large Line Spacing Compact Normal Spacious Comments Share Share Melanie McDonagh
Copied Linkedin Messenger Email Simon Baron-Cohen, the distinguished Cambridge autism specialist, has been speaking movingly about his friend, Jason Arday, in a BBC radio interview. Baron-Cohen said the last contact he had with Arday was hours before he was found dead at an address in south London yesterday afternoon: “He really wasn’t coping. He was being subjected to relentless scrutiny… ridicule, discrediting every detail of his life… He wasn’t coping with the loss of his career, the loss of his reputation. He felt he couldn’t go on.”
Jason Arday was a victim, but not in the way that his political champions suggest
Baron-Cohen went on to talk about him as “an incredibly kind and gentle and caring and generous man”. From his own perspective, he observed, “at the heart of all this was a man who was diagnosed with autism and language differences…he needed support every step of the way… after the allegations of plagiarism, [the] media didn’t leave him alone.”
It is good to be reminded of Jason Arday as a friend, by a friend. For in death we all should be remembered in our humanity, even in our flawed humanity. And Jason Arday was very human; he bled. He was not just a totem of DEI (Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion), but as the Prof said, a vulnerable man. It’s sometimes hard for pundits, self included, to remember how terrifying it is to be at the heart of a media firestorm. Jason Arday isn’t the first to feel the pressure to be unbearable. We may not feel exactly guilt at participating in the row, but it would be strange if we didn’t feel sober, chastened, by his tragic end.
De mortuis nil nisi bonum is a good motto, but in Arday’s case, the difficulty about speaking no evil of the dead is in disentangling the man, the human being, from the issue. And the issue was quite legitimate: the apparent dearth of scrutiny of his successive appointments, the uncritical and unquestioned acceptance of his work and his claims as, for instance, a fundraiser. His family, in their pain, has talked about him as the victim of misinformation. This isn’t, I would say, the whole case, though this isn’t the time to rehearse the details.
Before his death becomes weaponized – as it already risks being – in the culture wars, we should make one thing clear, as I, in fact, did before he died. It is that the problem was not Jason Arday; it was with the individuals who lionized him, who promoted him beyond his capacities, who raised him up prematurely to stellar heights at an age which would have been remarkable for anyone, regardless of ethnicity. It is the individuals behind the system which created Jason Arday, the poster image of DEI, who should be asking themselves some questions.
Arday can hardly be blamed for not resisting this inexorable trajectory. And, I would say, the fault is with Cambridge for making a dud subject like Education a faculty on the same level as history or natural sciences or classics. Jason Arday was a victim, but not quite in the way that his political champions suggest.
He was also a man, a father, a son, a brother and an uncle, as his family have said, and it is as such he is being mourned. Requiescat in pace.
Melanie McDonagh is an Irish journalist working in London.

items.title_zh: 杰森·阿尔代的悲剧
items.summary_zh: 本文讨论了杰森·阿尔代在面对媒体持续压力和职业生涯丧失时的困境。阿尔代被诊断为自闭症（autism）和语言障碍（language differences），在经历抄袭指控后，他感到无法承受来自媒体的无情审视和嘲笑，缺乏必要的支持。他失去了职业和声誉，内心深处感到绝望，认为自己无法继续前行。文章强调了在这种情况下，社会对有特殊需求人士的支持和理解的重要性。
items.l1_lead: 杰森·阿尔代因媒体压力和职业危机感到绝望，突显了社会对特殊需求人士支持与理解的重要性。
items.l2_summary:
杰森·阿尔代的悲剧揭示了在媒体压力和职业生涯丧失的双重打击下，特殊需求人士所面临的困境。阿尔代被诊断为自闭症（autism）和语言障碍（language differences），这使他在面对外界的审视时显得更加脆弱。在经历了抄袭指控后，媒体的持续关注和无情的嘲笑让他感到无所适从，缺乏必要的支持与理解。他的职业生涯因此受到重创，声誉也随之崩塌，内心深处的绝望感愈发加重，令他认为自己无法继续前行。

文章强调了社会对有特殊需求人士的支持和理解的重要性，指出在面对困境时，缺乏适当的帮助和关怀可能会导致更严重的心理和情感问题。阿尔代的经历不仅是个人的悲剧，更是对社会如何对待特殊需求人士的深刻反思。通过他的故事，读者能够感受到在职业生涯和个人生活中，理解与支持的重要性，以及在面对困难时，社会应当提供怎样的帮助。杰森·阿尔代的遭遇提醒我们，只有通过建立一个更具包容性和理解的环境，才能真正帮助那些在逆境中挣扎的人们。

items.claim_zh: 他认为夏威夷现有的桉树资源可以安全用于建筑，以满足社区的需求。
items.article_body:
August 10, 2026 UH News Reading time: 2 minutes
University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa researchers are working to determine whether Hawaiʻi -grown eucalyptus could become a reliable source of lumber for construction, helping reduce the state’s reliance on imported building materials while supporting healthier forests.
The project, led by Jun Wang, an assistant professor in the Department of Civil, Environmental and Construction Engineering , received a $300,000 USDA Forest Service Wood Innovation Grant to establish the engineering standards needed for eucalyptus to be used in structural applications.
Although Hawaiʻi has more than 34,000 acres of managed eucalyptus plantations, the wood is rarely used in construction because engineers and builders lack the design data needed to certify it for structural use. If successful, the research could create new opportunities for Hawaiʻi ’s forestry and wood products industries while reducing shipping costs, supply chain risks and carbon emissions associated with importing lumber. Researchers also say putting more eucalyptus to use could encourage better forest management by reducing excess wood that can contribute to wildfire fuel.
The research team will work with state agencies, forest landowners and industry partners to harvest trees, produce lumber and test its strength and durability. The findings will help establish engineering design values needed for commercial construction and could lay the groundwork for future engineered wood products made in Hawaiʻi .
“Our goal is to determine whether a resource that’s already growing in Hawaiʻi can safely be used to build the homes, schools and infrastructure our communities need,” Wang said. “If we can provide the engineering data the construction industry needs, we can help create a more resilient local building supply while giving our students the opportunity to solve real challenges facing Hawaiʻi .”
The research also will benefit students. Wang’s team received an $8,000 American Society for Engineering Education grant to incorporate Hawaiʻi -grown eucalyptus into civil engineering courses. The new curriculum will give students hands-on experience evaluating sustainable building materials by comparing locally grown eucalyptus with conventional construction materials.
Students will examine factors such as structural performance, carbon emissions and local sourcing while participating in research that addresses Hawaiʻi ’s unique environmental and construction challenges. Many members of the research team are UH students from Hawaiʻi who are helping develop solutions that could benefit the state’s future infrastructure and economy.
items.title_zh: 夏威夷桉树森林或成新建筑材料来源
items.summary_zh: 夏威夷大学系统的科学家们正在研究夏威夷现有的桉树资源是否可以安全地用于建筑，以满足社区对住房、学校和基础设施的需求。他们的目标是提供建筑行业所需的工程数据，从而帮助建立更具韧性的本地建筑材料供应。这不仅能解决夏威夷面临的实际挑战，还能为学生提供实践机会，培养他们的解决问题能力。科学家们认为，桉树作为一种可再生资源，具有潜力成为可持续建筑材料的来源。
items.l1_lead: 夏威夷大学的研究表明，桉树可作为可持续建筑材料，满足当地住房和基础设施需求，同时为学生提供实践机会。
items.l2_summary:
夏威夷大学系统的科学家们正在探索夏威夷现有的桉树（Eucalyptus）资源是否可以安全地用于建筑，以满足社区对住房、学校和基础设施的需求。随着夏威夷面临的住房危机和基础设施需求不断增加，寻找可持续的建筑材料显得尤为重要。研究团队的目标是提供建筑行业所需的工程数据，以支持建立更具韧性的本地建筑材料供应。这一研究不仅旨在解决实际的建筑需求，还为学生提供了实践机会，帮助他们培养解决问题的能力。

科学家们认为，桉树作为一种可再生资源，具有成为可持续建筑材料来源的潜力。通过对桉树的特性进行深入研究，团队希望能够确定其在建筑领域的应用安全性和有效性。这一研究不仅关注材料的物理性能，还将考虑环境影响和经济可行性，从而为夏威夷的建筑行业提供全面的支持。

在当前全球对可持续发展和绿色建筑材料需求日益增长的背景下，夏威夷的这一研究具有重要的现实意义。通过利用本地资源，夏威夷不仅可以减少对外部建筑材料的依赖，还能促进地方经济的发展，创造更多就业机会。总之，夏威夷大学的研究团队正在为未来的建筑行业开辟新的方向，推动可持续建筑材料的应用，助力社区建设与发展。

items.title: Introducing Biomni: Stanford’s AI co-scientist built to accelerate biomedical research - The Brighter Side of News
items.body:
原话：“If you think of an agent as a carpenter, a carpenter without tools is just a carpenter who can talk.” / “The hurdle in biomedical science is not intelligence or ideas; it is mechanics.” / “This difference is not just about efficiency. It changes how research can be done.”

论据：在40分钟内，Biomni清理了数据，结合了数据，创建了可视化，并识别了饮食与体温之间的联系。

items.article_body:
A new AI system called Biomni can design experiments, analyze data, and accelerate biomedical research in minutes. (CREDIT: Shutterstock)
Stanford University researchers developed Biomni, an AI “co-scientist” that can read scientific papers, analyze datasets, write and execute code, form hypotheses, and design experiments in minutes. Biomni uses 150 specialized tools, 105 software packages, and 59 databases across 25 areas of biology, allowing it to complete complex biomedical research tasks at speeds far beyond traditional human workflows. Researchers say Biomni is designed to augment rather than replace scientists, handling labor-intensive research tasks while leaving interpretation, creativity, and final decision-making to humans.
A new kind of scientific partner is beginning to take shape in research labs. It does not wear a lab coat or hold a pipette. Instead, it reads thousands of papers, writes code, analyzes data, and suggests new experiments in minutes. Researchers at Stanford University call it Biomni, an artificial intelligence system designed to act as a “co-scientist.”
The system, described in the journal Science , reflects a growing effort to rethink how research is done. As scientific knowledge expands, the challenge is no longer just having ideas. It is managing the enormous workload required to test them.
“If you think of an agent as a carpenter, a carpenter without tools is just a carpenter who can talk,” said Jure Leskovec, professor of computer science at Stanford. “With Biomni, we give the carpenter a set of tools, so it can build.”
Modern biomedical research moves at a fast pace. New studies appear daily, and datasets grow larger each year. Yet progress often slows under the weight of routine tasks.
Scientists must read literature, organize data, write code, and test ideas before reaching conclusions. Each step takes time. Together, they can delay discovery for weeks or months.
“The hurdle in biomedical science is not intelligence or ideas; it is mechanics,” Leskovec said. “It’s this laborious stuff that slows innovation. Biomni can do this work in minutes.”
This challenge has created a gap between what researchers know and what they can act on. Important patterns may remain hidden simply because there is not enough time to explore them.
Biomni was designed to close that gap. The idea is simple. A scientist should be able to ask a question in plain language and receive a complete research workflow in return.
The system reads scientific papers, forms hypotheses , selects datasets, and chooses the right tools. It writes and runs code, interprets results, and suggests next steps.
“Biomni is able to understand a simple question like, ‘Why are these patients responding differently to the drug?’” said Kexin Huang, who helped lead the project. “Then it digs in, doing a lot of the scientific legwork.”
This process turns a single question into a structured investigation. Instead of handling one task at a time, the system manages the entire pipeline from start to finish.
To achieve this, researchers built a large digital environment for the system. Biomni draws on full-text papers, code repositories, and datasets from across the biomedical field.
It includes 150 specialized tools, 105 software packages, and 59 databases. These resources span 25 areas of biology, from genetics to neuroscience.
The system identifies which tools are needed for a given task. It then combines them into a step-by-step plan. Each step is translated into code that can be executed automatically.
This design allows Biomni to adapt to many types of problems. It does not rely on a fixed workflow . Instead, it builds a new one for each question.
The system’s speed is one of its most striking features. In one real-world example, a researcher uploaded more than 450 files of health data. These included glucose levels, food intake, and physical activity.
The user asked a simple question. Analyze the data and find meaningful patterns.
Within 40 minutes, Biomni cleaned the data, combined it, created visualizations , and identified links between diet and body temperature. Leskovec said the same work could take a human more than 60 hours.
This difference is not just about efficiency. It changes how research can be done. Faster analysis allows scientists to test more ideas and explore more possibilities.
To evaluate performance, researchers tested Biomni on hundreds of biomedical questions. These included tasks such as gene identification and disease analysis.
The system performed well across these areas. In many cases, it matched the accuracy of experienced researchers. It also completed tasks much faster.
In one test involving rare disease diagnosis , Biomni reached 60 percent accuracy. This was similar to experts, who scored between 60 and 70 percent. However, the system finished the task in three minutes, while humans took nearly two hours.
In another test focused on gene detection, it achieved 80 percent accuracy. It reduced analysis time from about 90 minutes to just four minutes.
These results suggest that the system can support experts by handling time-consuming work.
Biomni does more than analyze data. It can also design experiments and guide laboratory work.
In one case, the system generated a complete protocol for DNA cloning . It included detailed steps, materials, and validation methods.
Researchers followed the instructions in the lab. The experiment worked as expected. Colonies grew, and DNA sequencing confirmed the results.
This ability to connect digital analysis with physical experiments is a key strength. It shows that the system can move from theory to practice.
Another advantage lies in how Biomni tracks its work. Every step is recorded and linked to sources.
The system provides full citations for the data and methods it uses. This allows researchers to verify results and reproduce findings.
In science, reproducibility is essential. By documenting its process, Biomni helps strengthen the reliability of research.
Despite its capabilities, researchers stress that Biomni is not meant to replace scientists.
The system can process information quickly and find patterns. However, it does not make final decisions. Human judgment remains central to the scientific process.
“And it always will,” Huang said. “This is not about machines taking over science, but more about machines becoming a powerful new partner to augment human researchers.”
The goal is to free scientists from routine tasks. This allows them to focus on creativity, interpretation, and decision-making .
The system still has limits. It does not cover every area of biology. Some tasks require more detailed input to ensure accuracy.
Researchers are working to expand its capabilities. Future versions may include more data sources and improved reasoning methods.
There are also questions about safety. Tools that can design experiments must be used responsibly. Developers emphasize the importance of transparency and ethical guidelines .
Even with these challenges, early adoption is strong. More than 10,000 labs have begun using the system in academic and industry settings.
The rise of systems like Biomni reflects a broader shift in research. As knowledge grows, collaboration between humans and machines becomes more important.
Instead of working alone, scientists may rely on digital partners that handle complex workflows . This could speed up discovery and open new paths for innovation.
For fields like medicine, the impact could be profound. Faster research may lead to quicker development of treatments and deeper understanding of disease.
This work could transform how biomedical research is conducted. By automating routine tasks, it allows scientists to focus on deeper questions and creative thinking. This may accelerate discoveries in areas such as drug development and disease prevention.
The system also lowers barriers to entry. Researchers with fewer resources can access advanced tools and perform complex analyses. This could expand participation in science and increase global collaboration.
In healthcare, faster data analysis may improve patient outcomes. Researchers can identify patterns more quickly and develop targeted treatments. Over time, this may lead to more personalized medicine.
For the scientific community, improved transparency and reproducibility strengthen trust in research. By documenting every step, the system helps ensure that findings can be verified and built upon.
Research findings are available online in the journal Science .
The original story " Introducing Biomni: Stanford’s AI co-scientist built to accelerate biomedical research " is published in The Brighter Side of News.

items.topic_zh: 对脆弱个体的支持与保护
items.claim_zh: 阿尔代在成长过程中作为一个脆弱的个体，应该得到每一步的保护和支持。
items.article_body:
Jason Arday was found dead at his home in south London on Friday. Photograph: Christian Sinibaldi/The Guardian View image in fullscreen Jason Arday was found dead at his home in south London on Friday. Photograph: Christian Sinibaldi/The Guardian Jason Arday This article is more than 1 month old Tributes paid to Jason Arday after former Cambridge professor’s death This article is more than 1 month old Andy Burnham calls for reflection after ‘tragedy on so many levels’ in comments echoed by London mayor Sadiq Khan
Prefer the Guardian on Google Andy Burnham has called the death of Jason Arday , whose body was found at his home in south London on Friday, a “tragedy on so many levels”.
Arday resigned as a professor at the University of Cambridge last week after allegations of plagiarism, which he denied. He was pronounced dead just after 3pm on Friday .
In a statement issued via his publisher, Simon & Schuster UK, the former academic’s family said they were “in shock to have lost this amazing father, partner, brother, uncle and son”.
Speaking to broadcasters during a visit to Cornwall on Saturday, the prime minister said: “It’s a tragedy on so many levels, but particularly just for everybody who knew Jason, his family obviously, his friends. We think of them today.
“It’s not a moment for any rushing to judgment. It’s a moment for reflection, I would say, reflecting on how things came to this. A really sad, sad and sorry state of affairs and I think we all today think of Jason, his contribution and his family and friends.”
More than £20,000 has been raised for the family of Arday after the Windrush campaigner Sir Patrick Vernon launched a fundraising drive via GoFundMe in his memory.
Other leading figures to pay tribute included the London mayor, Sadiq Khan, and the Labour MP Bell Ribeiro-Addy.
Khan said: “I’m devastated for the family and friends of Jason Arday. He faced an unacceptable public hounding and campaign of abuse. I know many Londoners will be angry and upset this evening.
“Jason Arday was the victim of a pernicious public shaming that other people in his position simply wouldn’t have faced. His death was a tragedy, but once again it should be a wake-up call for all of us.”
Speaking on Newsnight, Ribeiro-Addy read out a list of names including William O’Reilly, Ros Holmes, David Latchman, and Nicola Morrison. “These are all people that have actually proven to have been plagiarists, or people that have manipulated their data, and people that have been proven to have lifted whole pages from students’ papers or published work that they had to withdraw,” she said.
Ribeiro-Addy said there had been a media witch-hunt which was cruel because “it didn’t aim to just target him”.
“It aimed to target anybody that supported him, trying to isolate him as much as possible, going after people who had signed up to statements,” she said. “The difference between them and him was they were white, and he was not.”
The Conservative MP James Cleverly expressed his anger over Arday’s death. In a statement on X, he wrote that a number of people at academic institutions “have serious questions to answer”.
“They put him into positions he was clearly not qualified for so they could have a black wunderkind to show off, they pushed him into the spotlight for their own benefit,” they said. “His exposure was inevitable, a case of when, not if. His whole world fell apart.”
Simon Baron-Cohen, a clinical psychologist and the director of the Autism Research Centre, who was a friend of Arday’s, told Radio 4’s Today programme that he contacted him Friday morning and said that he felt he was unable to go on.
“He used those words in voice notes,” Baron-Cohen said. “At the heart of all of this was a man who’d been diagnosed in childhood with disabilities that included autism and language delay and learning differences.
“He was a vulnerable child, a vulnerable teenager and a vulnerable adult, so he needed and deserved safeguarding and support and reasonable adjustment every step of the way.”
Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to First Edition
Our morning email breaks down the key stories of the day, telling you what’s happening and why it matters
Arday was initially accused of plagiarising another person’s work in his PhD thesis, but denied all allegations. A review conducted by Liverpool John Moores University, where he completed his doctorate, upheld its decision to award him a PhD earlier this year.
In recent weeks, other elements of his life story were increasingly questioned , including claims of prodigious money-raising for charity and feats of long-distance running. He was also challenged about whether he was nonverbal as a child.
The National Education Union general secretary, Daniel Kebede, said Arday had been subjected to “a public and brutal takedown that unleashed a tirade of racism”.
“I don’t believe this was ever simply about ‘professional conduct’ or ‘plagiarism’,” he said.
“There is a profound difference between scrutiny and a sustained public campaign that turns an individual into a symbol of everything the right believes is wrong with DEI.
“The effect has been chilling. It tells Black people and others from underrepresented backgrounds that entering prominent public positions will make you a target.
“A target not only for criticism of your work, but for a much broader political and cultural backlash.”
The Metropolitan police said his death was being treated as unexpected, but not believed to be suspicious.
In the UK and Ireland, Samaritans can be contacted on freephone 116 123. In the US, you can call or text the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline at 988 or chat at 988lifeline.org . In Australia, the crisis support service Lifeline is 13 11 14. Other international helplines can be found at befrienders.org
This article was amended on 16 August 2026 to correct the spelling of the names of Ros Holmes and David Latchman.
items.title_zh: 阿尔代：脆弱个体的保护与支持
items.summary_zh: 文章讨论了已故剑桥大学教授阿尔代的成长经历，强调他在童年时期被诊断出自闭症、语言延迟和学习差异等障碍。作者指出，阿尔代作为一个脆弱的孩子、青少年和成年人，始终需要并应当得到保护、支持和合理的调整。文章的核心论点是，社会应为像阿尔代这样的脆弱个体提供必要的保障，以确保他们在成长过程中能够获得平等的机会和支持。

items.l2_summary:
阿尔代（Alday）是已故剑桥大学教授，他的成长经历为我们提供了对脆弱个体保护与支持的重要思考。文章指出，阿尔代在童年时期被诊断出自闭症（Autism）、语言延迟（Language Delay）和学习差异（Learning Differences），这些障碍使他在生活的各个阶段都面临着挑战。作为一个脆弱的孩子、青少年和成年人，阿尔代始终需要保护和支持，这不仅是他个人的需求，也是社会应承担的责任。

文章的核心论点强调，社会应为像阿尔代这样的脆弱个体提供必要的保障，以确保他们在成长过程中能够获得平等的机会和支持。阿尔代的经历表明，缺乏适当的支持和合理的调整，脆弱个体可能会面临更大的困难和孤立。因此，社会各界应当关注这些个体的需求，提供必要的资源和环境，以帮助他们克服障碍，实现自我价值。

通过对阿尔代的成长故事的分析，作者呼吁社会重视脆弱个体的权益，倡导建立一个包容的环境，使每一个人都能在平等的基础上获得发展机会。这样的支持不仅有助于脆弱个体的成长，也将促进整个社会的和谐与进步。总之，阿尔代的经历提醒我们，保护和支持脆弱个体是社会的共同责任，只有通过集体的努力，才能为他们创造一个更加友好的生活和学习环境。

George Brown: the former Post Office boy who unlocked the mystery of depression
Derek Owusu: ‘I’ve never figured out how to live in the world’
Two weeks ago, following a conversation with Jason Arday, Professor Simon Baron-Cohen posted a message on X.
The psychologist said he was “very concerned” about the impact of media coverage on his friend, who had autism, and linked it to work his Autism Research Centre at Cambridge University had done showing that autistic people were at a greater risk of suicide.
“This is relentless bullying of a vulnerable autistic man and raises safe-guarding issues,” he wrote. “It’s time to stop.” The site’s owner, Elon Musk, responded to the post with one word: “Liar”.
Yesterday, Baron-Cohen said Arday had sent him a voice note via WhatsApp on the morning of his death. “He was being subjected to relentless scrutiny, including ridicule, discrediting absolutely every detail of his life, and he wasn’t coping with… he felt he couldn’t go on,” he told Radio 4’s Today programme.
In 2022, Baron-Cohen and psychologists from other UK universities found that autistic people had an elevated risk of suicide. They examined 372 coroners’ inquest reports over a three-year period to find out whether the person who died had been diagnosed with autism or had autistic traits. They found evidence of autism in more than 10% of those who died, compared with about 1.1% of the population overall.
Jill Aylott, founder of the National Autism and ADHD Assessment Centre, said: “accountability should never require us to abandon humanity.
“When somebody becomes the focus of sustained national criticism, particularly where that person is known to be neurodivergent, institutions should be asking: who is checking that this person is safe?”
Baron-Cohen said that for the last 10 days he had seen Arday’s mental health “getting worse and worse”.

Derek Owusu: ‘I’ve never figured out how to live in the world’
“We need to let the investigations proceed. We need to understand how this tragedy has happened, but there has to be accountability at lots of levels.”

items.title: Hawaii to Put Thirty Years of Eucalyptus Through Load Testing - Wood Central
items.body:
原话：“We can help create a more resilient local building supply.”
论点：他认为通过研究可以增强夏威夷的建筑材料供应的韧性。
论据：Wang’s team has $300,000 to produce numbers no one has generated over the three decades those trees have been standing.
items.authors: Jun Wang
items.attribution_basis: Google News 全名命中 + LLM 同一人核验（Wood Central） + 论点方向独立复核
quotes: We can help create a more resilient local building supply.
items.topic_zh: 关于增强当地建筑材料供应的观点
items.claim_zh: 他认为通过研究可以增强夏威夷的建筑材料供应的韧性。
items.evidence_zh: Wang’s team has $300,000 to produce numbers no one has generated over the three decades those trees have been standing.
items.article_body:
Eucalyptus stands across more than 34,000 acres of Hawaiʻi’s old sugar land, or 13,760 hectares, and no published data exists to tell a builder what a plank of lumber can hold. However, that could soon change thanks to a new University of Hawaiʻi project , which will see the USDA Forest Service provide US$300,000 to generate structural design values for the species, with the project to fell the trees, saw the boards, and test them.
“We can help create a more resilient local building supply,” said Jun Wang, an assistant professor in the university’s Department of Civil, Environmental and Construction Engineering, whose team will run the work with state agencies, forest landowners, and industry partners. Wang has taken an additional $8,000 from the American Society for Engineering Education to incorporate the same material into civil engineering coursework at Mānoa.
Hawaiʻi’s large landowners put those trees into former cane land through the 1990s, holding tens of thousands of Hāmakua Coast acres off the property market , with agreements drawn to sell the crop to Oji Paper and Marubeni , the Japanese consortium that would chip it for paper. Hawaiian authorities rejected a 1997 lease over 4,150 hectares of public land after local opposition. The ventures that followed came and went, and the trees stayed.
Engineers cannot specify a beam without published design values, and no building official approves a species for load-bearing work until those numbers exist, regardless of what the timber does in a test rig. Eucalyptus grandis and E. saligna dominate the Hāmakua stands, which Mālama Hāmakua reports foresters rate suitable for flooring, structural, veneer, and ply work.
Distributors on the islands hold two to four weeks of stock compared with eight to 12 weeks on the mainland, so a West Coast price rise reaches an island invoice inside a fortnight, according to Associated Builders and Contractors Hawaiʻi. The same association puts local sourcing at under 20 per cent of the state’s building material needs, with the balance requiring an ocean crossing before reaching a site.
No mill on Hawaiʻi Island runs at the scale that would put eucalyptus boards alongside imported product on price, and the island’s hardwood mills stay with high-value koa to turn a profit, on Mālama Hāmakua’s account of what foresters told it. The wood that did leave between 2012 and 2016 went to China as veneer material before that market fell away, and a Waiakea mill licensed to peel the species never reached the volumes proposed.
It comes as Australian researchers turned plantation bluegum grown for pulp into structural glulam in February, the same class of timber used for the same purpose, with a Portland hub costing $200 million proposed to make the product at scale. Grading the timber and building the mill are separate bills, and only the first has been funded in Hawaiʻi.
Fire has given the state a second argument for cutting the stands, with the Department of Land and Natural Resources estimating that the 2012 Kōkeʻe wildfires released 72,000 tonnes of carbon, which it compares to the annual emissions of 18,000 cars. Those fires burned more than 3,000 acres of a Timber Management Area that covers 17,092 acres and holds more than 1,600 acres of eucalyptus and pine.
The department built a house from these species eight years ago, with Hale Liʻi framed in Sydney gum, rose gum, and southern yellow pine cut from Kōkeʻe on Kauaʻi and Hāmakua on Hawaiʻi Island. That 2018 grant came from the same federal Wood Innovations programme, and the 400-square-foot result is one nobody can yet repeat at commercial scale.
Wang’s team has $300,000 to produce numbers no one has generated over the three decades those trees have been standing, on an estate the university puts at over 34,000 acres. Design values will settle whether Hawaiʻi’s eucalyptus can be built with, and a mill will settle whether it ever is.

items.title: Warnings about Jason Arday’s mental health were ignored by the press - Good Law Project
items.body:
原话：“I’m very concerned about the impact of the media coverage on Jason Arday who is autistic.”
论点：媒体对自闭症人士Jason Arday的报道可能产生负面影响。
items.authors: Simon Baron‐Cohen
items.attribution_basis: Google News 全名命中 + LLM 同一人核验（Good Law Project） + 论点方向独立复核
quotes: I’m very concerned about the impact of the media coverage on Jason Arday who is autistic.
items.topic_zh: 媒体报道对自闭症人士的影响
items.claim_zh: 媒体对自闭症人士Jason Arday的报道可能产生负面影响。
items.article_body:
We use cookies where necessary to allow us to understand how people interact with our website and content, so that we can continue to improve our service.
Dr Arday’s death was the direct result of media harassment – we’re demanding a public inquiry to prevent this from ever happening again
Before his death on Friday, Dr Jason Arday was subject to a barrage of racist, ableist and cruel media attention, which continued to escalate even after his resignation on August 5th.
The press attention was unrelenting. 249 articles were published in 22 days, mostly led by the broadsheets. This wasn’t a tabloid scandal – the journalists involved were often public figures in their own right.
A resignation normally causes the media to back off, but they only produced more content. Stories about Jason were driving clicks – with outlets like The Times even putting out paid adverts for their articles .
In his resignation letter, Dr Jason Arday said to his supporters “you have carried me through some of the darkest moments of my life”; “I need time to heal”; “space to begin again” and that he had “reached the limits of what any person should reasonably be expected to endure.”
Jason wasn’t the only one asking the press to stop.
Professor Simon Baron Cohen released a statement on July 31st, leaning on his expertise in autism, stating:
“I’m very concerned about the impact of the media coverage on Professor Jason Arday who is autistic.
He has been accused of plagiarism and he was cleared of any academic misconduct following a rigorous investigation by Liverpool John Moores University.
And yet he continues to be systematically discredited over every detail of his life, daily. We should of course always investigate plagiarism to protect academic standards.
However, I cannot stand by and watch when an autistic man is on the ground and the kicking continues. This is relentless bullying of a vulnerable autistic man and raises safe-guarding issues. It’s time to stop.”
The day afterwards, the Guardian published an article titled “Playbooks, plagiarism and a pig’s head: new claims surrounding a star Cambridge professor”.
Before this article was published, details of it were sent to Jason to give him an opportunity to respond. His supporters contacted The Guardian about this piece. A letter was sent to Katharine Viner, the Editor-in-Chief of the Guardian, and separate contact was made with the journalist writing the piece.
This article dissected Jason’s claims about his personal life, and the Guardian featured it on their podcast, Today In Focus. A reel the Guardian posted of that podcast, where the claims within the article were played for laughs, has since been deleted.
The Guardian’s coverage continued after Arday’s resignation, interviewing people who knew Jason as a child to question whether he was really non-verbal. The intense focus on Jason’s background and disability was widespread, with The Daily Mail even carrying a piece from a psychiatrist pondering a diagnosis for Jason, tempered only by the context that “I should say that I’ve never met Jason Arday, and so have no idea what has been going on in his mind, or how much truth there may or may not be in his life story.”
During the escalating coverage, those who supported Arday received countless requests for interviews and quotes.
These journalists were often warned about Jason’s wellbeing, and were still not dissuaded from chasing the story.
The writer and broadcaster Nels Abbey and Lord Simon Woolley , the Principal of Homerton College, both expressed their concerns.
Nels shared an example of this type of correspondence from the 3rd of August with a journalist during the firestorm, explicitly making clear his concern for Jason’s wellbeing.
Despite warnings from those around Jason trying to safeguard him from the onslaught, the stories kept coming.
Hours after Jason died, The Times ran a (now deleted) story headlined “Jason Arday may want to get himself a nice pair of orange trousers”.
Whilst this continued, the racist and eugenist academic Nathan Cofnas, who instigated the story, gave a little remarked upon interview to a right-wing youtuber, joking: “ After the revolution, I’ll be the head of the dept of eugenics & race science at Harvard.”
We believe that the press must be held accountable for their racist, profit-motivated conduct that led to Jason’s death. We’re calling for a public inquiry into how to ensure a responsible press given its contribution to Dr Arday’s tragic death.

items.title_zh: 媒体忽视Jason Arday心理健康警告的影响
items.summary_zh: 本文讨论了媒体对自闭症人士Jason Arday的报道可能带来的负面影响。文章引用了对Arday心理健康的担忧，指出媒体在报道中未能充分考虑其自闭症（autism）背景，可能加剧了对其的误解和偏见。专家强调，媒体的关注应更加谨慎，以避免对Arday及其他自闭症人士造成伤害。整体而言，文章呼吁媒体在报道此类敏感话题时，需更加关注受影响者的心理健康和社会影响。
items.l1_lead: 媒体在报道自闭症人士Jason Arday时忽视其心理健康背景，可能加剧误解与偏见，呼吁更谨慎的报道以保护受影响者。
items.l2_summary:
本文探讨了媒体对自闭症人士Jason Arday的报道可能带来的负面影响，特别是对其心理健康的潜在威胁。文章指出，媒体在报道中未能充分考虑Arday的自闭症背景，导致对他的误解和偏见加剧。专家们强调，媒体在关注此类敏感话题时，应更加谨慎，以避免对Arday及其他自闭症人士造成进一步的伤害。报道中提到的心理健康担忧，反映了社会对自闭症人士的普遍误解，这种误解不仅影响了公众对他们的看法，也可能对他们的心理健康产生负面影响。

整体而言，文章呼吁媒体在报道涉及自闭症及相关心理健康问题时，需更加关注受影响者的心理健康和社会影响。通过对Arday案例的分析，作者希望引起媒体和公众对自闭症人士心理健康问题的重视，促使媒体在报道时采取更为负责任的态度，以减少对自闭症人士的偏见和误解。

items.title: Cambridge professor says university should continue Jason Arday investigation - The Independent
items.body:
原话：“They have announced an investigation, and we should let that proceed.”
论点：大学应该让对Jason Arday的调查继续进行。
items.authors: Simon Baron‐Cohen
items.attribution_basis: Google News 全名命中 + LLM 同一人核验（The Independent） + 论点方向独立复核
quotes: They have announced an investigation, and we should let that proceed.
items.topic_zh: 关于大学对Jason Arday事件的调查
items.claim_zh: 大学应该让对Jason Arday的调查继续进行。
items.article_body:
A fundraiser for Prof Arday’s family, set up by Windrush campaigner Sir Patrick Vernon, has raised more than £60,000
Bookmark Bookmark popover Removed from bookmarks
Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.
From reproductive rights to climate change to Big Tech, The Independent is on the ground when the story is developing. Whether it's investigating the financials of Elon Musk's pro-Trump PAC or producing our latest documentary, 'The A Word', which shines a light on the American women fighting for reproductive rights, we know how important it is to parse out the facts from the messaging.
At such a critical moment in US history, we need reporters on the ground. Your donation allows us to keep sending journalists to speak to both sides of the story.
The Independent is trusted by Americans across the entire political spectrum. And unlike many other quality news outlets, we choose not to lock Americans out of our reporting and analysis with paywalls. We believe quality journalism should be available to everyone, paid for by those who can afford it.
The University of Cambridge ought to proceed with its probe into how Professor Jason Arday was recruited and his period teaching at the institution, according to a friend and former colleague.
Prof Arday, who was found dead on Friday, stepped down from his post as professor of sociology of education last week following allegations of plagiarism made against him.
Prior to his death, the university stated that it would look into the circumstances surrounding his "appointment and tenure", with the conclusions feeding into a wider review of senior recruitment processes.
It is understood that the university currently feels it would not be right to decide whether to continue the inquiry while Prof Arday’s family is grieving.
Sir Simon Baron-Cohen, a friend and former colleague of Prof Arday, told Times Radio that the university should "always be reflecting on how it’s operating and whether it can do better".
The Cambridge professor and director of the Autism Research Centre said: “They have announced an investigation, and we should let that proceed.
“We should we should see what we learn from it. This is the whole purpose of investigations.
“When you’re talking about what’s in the public interest, when you’ve got public bodies like universities or, arguably, the media, political institutions, whatever, when we have investigations, it’s all about how can we improve them.”
Sir Simon said the professor’s mental health had been left “in tatters”, adding there were questions about whether the media failed in its duty of care towards him as a vulnerable person with disabilities.
He said the professor faced racist abuse and was used as a “lightning rod for a culture war on DEI (diversity, equity and inclusion)”.
“(Prof Arday) started reporting racism within weeks of him being at Cambridge,” Sir Simon said.
“It included things like threats of physical assault to himself and his family, racist hate speech, and racist actions, hate actions.”
Lord Simon Woolley, principal of Homerton College, Cambridge, and a former mentor of Prof Arday, told BBC Radio 4’s Broadcasting House programme that his friend felt “hounded to death”.
Lord Woolley said: “In a conversation I had with Jason on the Monday – we met on Monday, with a few dear friends – he said he felt hounded to death, his words, that he couldn’t see a way out.”
He added: “On that day, we saw a man half his body weight and desperate beyond belief.”
The crossbench peer said Prof Arday had been subjected to “the most horrendous, toxic, vicious witch hunt”, and called for an investigation into the “vicious media onslaught”.
“The whole of the black community and black academics have been brought into this debate as though we don’t belong in these positions, because we are collectively the diversity, equity and inclusion hires,” Lord Woolley added.
A fundraiser for Prof Arday’s family, set up by Windrush campaigner Sir Patrick Vernon, has raised more than £60,000.
The organisation Stand Up To Racism has announced plans for a vigil for Prof Arday to be held on the steps of the National Gallery in Trafalgar Square, central London, at 6pm on Monday.
On Saturday, Prime Minister Andy Burnham described the professor’s death as a “tragedy on so many levels”, adding: “It’s not a moment for any rushing to judgment. It’s a moment for reflection, I would say, reflecting on how things came to this.”
In a statement issued by his publisher Simon & Schuster UK on Friday, Prof Arday’s family said he had been subjected to a “campaign of sustained abuse” since he accepted the role of professor at Cambridge.
They said: “The campaign of misinformation was too much for Jason, who was a gentle man and who always wanted to see the best in everyone.”
items.title_zh: 剑桥教授支持继续对Jason Arday的调查
items.summary_zh: 剑桥大学的一位教授表示，大学应继续对Jason Arday的调查。他指出，调查已经启动，应该让其顺利进行，以确保公正和透明。这一观点强调了学术界在处理类似事件时应保持的严谨态度，确保所有相关问题得到充分审查。教授的发言反映了对学术诚信的重视，认为调查的结果将对大学的声誉和未来发展产生重要影响。
items.l1_lead: 剑桥大学教授支持继续对Jason Arday的调查，强调学术界应保持严谨态度，确保公正透明，以维护学术诚信和大学声誉。
items.l2_summary: 剑桥大学的一位教授近日表示，大学应继续对Jason Arday的调查，以确保这一过程的公正和透明。他强调，调查已经启动，应该顺利进行，以便对所有相关问题进行充分审查。这一观点反映了学术界在处理类似事件时所应保持的严谨态度，突显了对学术诚信的重视。教授认为，调查的结果不仅关乎个体的声誉，更将对大学的整体声誉和未来发展产生重要影响。因此，继续推进调查显得尤为重要，以确保所有相关问题都能得到妥善处理，维护学术界的信任和公信力。

items.title: Polymeric Sorbents as Energy-Efficient Alternative to Cryogenic Distillation for Light Hydrocarbon Purification.
items.body: Light hydrocarbons are essential gaseous compounds for fuel, polymer manufacturing, fertilizer production, and so forth. The efficient recovery and purification of these gases are still challenging despite their significant industrial and domestic relevance. They exist in the gaseous state under ambient temperature and pressure and are typically recovered from natural gas streams containing multiple close-boiling-point hydrocarbons. So far, cryogenic distillation is the commonly used method for their separation and purification. It operates based on their boiling-point differences, which amounts to significant energy consumption. To address this limitation, adsorption-based technology is considered an energy-efficient alternative for the purification of light hydrocarbons. To this effect, polymeric sorbents such as porous polymer networks (PPNs) are a potential alternative due to their robustness, stability, and scalability. This review provides an extensive discussion on cryogenic distillation, applications of light hydrocarbons, and progress in light hydrocarbon purification using polymeric sorbents. Additionally, the pore structure, stability, and techno-economic feasibility of the polymeric sorbents were extensively examined, covering current progress, mechanism of guest molecule separation, characterization techniques, and hurdles still encountered. Overall, since their application in light hydrocarbon separation is still an evolving field, this review will facilitate robust designs by providing the necessary know-how and roadmaps needed for advancement.
items.authors: Festus K, Mondal A, Mandal S, Aiya D Marquez J, Ghosh A, Sikdar A, Podder U, Sarkar A, Wang Q, Zhou HC.
items.title_zh: 聚合物吸附剂作为轻烃净化的节能替代方案
items.summary_zh: 轻烃是燃料、聚合物制造和肥料生产等重要气体化合物，其高效回收和净化仍面临挑战。尽管轻烃在常温常压下以气态存在，通常从含有多种沸点接近的烃类的天然气流中回收，目前常用的分离和净化方法是低温蒸馏（cryogenic distillation），但该方法消耗大量能源。为了解决这一问题，基于吸附的技术被认为是轻烃净化的节能替代方案。聚合物吸附剂，如多孔聚合物网络（PPNs），因其稳健性、稳定性和可扩展性而成为潜在选择。本文广泛讨论了低温蒸馏、轻烃的应用以及使用聚合物吸附剂进行轻烃净化的进展。同时，深入研究了聚合物吸附剂的孔结构、稳定性和技术经济可行性，涵盖了当前进展、客体分子分离机制、表征技术及仍面临的挑战。
items.l1_lead: 聚合物吸附剂作为轻烃净化的节能替代方案，展现出良好的稳定性和可扩展性，有望解决传统低温蒸馏的高能耗问题。
items.l2_summary:
轻烃是燃料、聚合物制造和肥料生产等重要气体化合物，其高效回收和净化仍面临诸多挑战。轻烃在常温常压下以气态存在，通常从含有多种沸点接近的烃类的天然气流中回收。目前，低温蒸馏（cryogenic distillation）是常用的分离和净化方法，但该方法消耗大量能源，导致其在经济性和环境可持续性方面受到质疑。为了解决这一问题，基于吸附的技术被认为是轻烃净化的节能替代方案。

聚合物吸附剂，特别是多孔聚合物网络（PPNs），因其优越的稳健性、稳定性和可扩展性而成为潜在的选择。本文广泛讨论了低温蒸馏的局限性、轻烃的应用以及使用聚合物吸附剂进行轻烃净化的最新进展。研究表明，聚合物吸附剂的孔结构和稳定性对其净化性能至关重要，且其技术经济可行性也在不断提升。

在对聚合物吸附剂的研究中，作者深入探讨了客体分子分离机制及其表征技术，揭示了聚合物吸附剂在轻烃净化中的应用潜力。同时，文章也指出了当前技术仍面临的一些挑战，包括吸附剂的选择性、再生能力及其在实际应用中的表现等。通过对这些因素的综合分析，本文强调了聚合物吸附剂作为轻烃净化的节能替代方案的前景，展望了未来在这一领域的研究方向和发展潜力。

items.title: How will this year’s record breaking El Niño affect NZ and the world? 5 things to know
items.body: From global temperature records to drought risk in New Zealand, the developing climate pattern could have far-reaching consequences.
items.authors: Kevin E. Trenberth
items.attribution_basis: The Conversation 作者页 /profiles/kevin-trenberth-15259（名+姓双命中）
items.title_zh: 今年创纪录的厄尔尼诺现象将如何影响新西兰及全球？
items.summary_zh: 本文探讨了正在发展的厄尔尼诺现象（El Niño）对全球气温和新西兰干旱风险的潜在影响。厄尔尼诺现象是指赤道太平洋海水温度异常升高的气候模式，可能导致全球气温创下新高，并加剧新西兰的干旱风险。文章指出，这一气候模式的变化不仅影响局部气候，还可能对农业、生态系统和水资源管理产生深远影响。科学家们警告，随着厄尔尼诺现象的发展，各国需做好应对气候变化的准备，以减轻其带来的负面后果。
items.l1_lead: 厄尔尼诺现象将导致全球气温上升和新西兰干旱风险加剧，影响农业和水资源管理，需各国做好应对准备。
items.l2_summary:
今年，正在发展的厄尔尼诺现象（El Niño）引发了全球气候变化的广泛关注，尤其是对新西兰的干旱风险的潜在影响。厄尔尼诺现象是指赤道太平洋海水温度异常升高的气候模式，这种现象通常会导致全球气温的显著上升，甚至可能创下新高。文章指出，厄尔尼诺现象的变化不仅会影响局部气候，还可能对农业、生态系统和水资源管理产生深远的影响。

在新西兰，厄尔尼诺现象的影响尤为明显，气候模式的变化可能导致该国面临更高的干旱风险。这种干旱风险的增加将对农业生产造成直接威胁，影响粮食安全和农民的生计。此外，生态系统也可能受到影响，水资源的管理将变得更加复杂，尤其是在水资源本就紧张的地区。科学家们警告，随着厄尔尼诺现象的发展，各国需要做好应对气候变化的准备，以减轻其带来的负面后果。

总的来说，厄尔尼诺现象的出现不仅是一个气候事件，更是一个全球性挑战，要求各国采取积极措施应对气候变化带来的影响。新西兰作为受影响的国家之一，必须认真对待这一现象，制定相应的政策和措施，以应对可能出现的干旱和其他气候相关问题。
items.l3_translation:
距离预计的高峰还有几个月，厄尔尼诺现象已经在推动海洋温度达到创纪录的水平。

七月的全球海面温度达到了该月份有记录以来的最高值，部分原因是这一快速发展的气候模式。最新的预测表明，未来还有更多变化在等待着我们。

那么，厄尔尼诺究竟是什么？为什么这次的厄尔尼诺可能如此重要？它对新西兰又意味着什么？以下是五个需要了解的要点。

厄尔尼诺是一种自然气候模式，涉及中部和东部热带太平洋海域的异常升温，并伴随着风和大气环流的变化。

这个过程通常是这样运作的：太阳加热热带海洋，而信风则将温暖的表层水向西推送，导致其在印度尼西亚、北澳大利亚和东南亚附近堆积。与此同时，东太平洋的冷水从下方上升。

这种堆积意味着西太平洋“暖池”的海平面平均比南美东部的海平面高出约60厘米。如果没有信风将其保持在那里，这些温暖的水将会向东流动。但堆积的量是有限的。

厄尔尼诺的启动方式各不相同，天气和热带风暴有时会削弱信风并提供触发因素。一旦开始，温暖的水开始向东涌动，穿越太平洋。

穿越海洋可能需要两到三个月的时间，在此过程中会改变雷暴和降雨，并影响远超热带太平洋的天气模式。

厄尔尼诺事件通常每两到七年发生一次，最常见的是每三到五年发生一次。海温通常在十二月达到峰值，而最大的气候效应通常出现在次年的二月。

到2025年12月，热带太平洋已经为厄尔尼诺做好了准备。与热带风暴相关的西风脉冲帮助启动了这一过程，随后的涌动进一步加强了朝向南美的升温。

今年年初，重大事件的迹象开始显现。前新西兰国家水与大气研究所气象学家Ben Noll在二月提出了这一可能性，到七月时警告说这可能会成为一个非常强的——或称为“超级”——厄尔尼诺。

当前的预测表明，这一事件将在年底前继续增强，热带太平洋关键区域的海面温度将达到超过平均值3°C的创纪录水平。

厄尔尼诺的展开是在人为造成的升温背景下进行的，全球海洋热含量在2017年至2025年的每一年都达到了创纪录的水平。

1997-98年的厄尔尼诺事件使1998年成为20世纪最热的一年。2015-16年的厄尔尼诺将温度推向了另一个水平，而在2023-24年事件期间，记录再次被刷新。

强厄尔尼诺事件将一些积累的海洋热量释放到大气中，暂时提升全球表面温度。因此，全球温度可以看作是一个阶梯，主要的厄尔尼诺事件帮助将其推向更高的台阶。

这一正在发展的厄尔尼诺可能提供下一个台阶，2026年全球温度可能创下新高，2027年更有可能。

气候变化如何影响厄尔尼诺仍然不确定。但有迹象表明，升温可能正在改变这一现象本身，可能增加非常强事件的风险。

厄尔尼诺对全球产生深远影响，影响干旱、洪水、风暴和热浪，以及农业、健康、渔业、野火风险和经济活动。

一些影响已经显现。干旱条件扰乱了东南亚和中美洲部分地区的作物，而联合国世界粮食计划署估计，厄尔尼诺可能使到年底将近5000万人面临急性饥饿。

厄尔尼诺的全球影响很大程度上来自其对降雨的影响。热带太平洋异常高的海面温度将降雨向海洋转移，通常在陆地上造成干旱。这些变化改变了大气环流和更远地区的天气模式，同时增加了干旱地区的野火风险。

温度和降雨的变化可能影响诸如疟疾、登革热和霍乱等疾病。厄尔尼诺还会改变热带气旋的活动，通常在太平洋的中部和东部增加活动，而在热带大西洋则抑制活动。

南美沿岸的上升流减弱也减少了冷却、富含营养的水的供应，扰乱了海洋生态系统，并可能导致渔业和海鸟种群的急剧下降。

经济影响可能持续多年，造成数万亿美元的损失。

新西兰已经经历了一些厄尔尼诺的影响，包括在这个冬季大部分时间里相对阳光明媚但寒冷的南风条件。

与世界许多地方不同，新西兰在厄尔尼诺期间通常经历较冷的气候。

最强的影响通常在年末显现。在塔斯曼海对面，它可能导致澳大利亚大部分地区的干旱和野火风险，火灾产生的烟雾有时会飘到新西兰。

厄尔尼诺往往给新西兰的东北部地区带来更干燥的条件，特别是北岛，而西南部——包括峡湾地区和西海岸——则可能变得更湿润。

鉴于这一事件的潜在强度，新西兰面临所谓“干旱年”的真实风险，这将对农业和水电发电产生影响，并增加野火的风险。

农民和其他面临这些风险的人应为干旱的可能性做好准备。

杰出学者，国家大气研究中心；奥克兰大学附属教员，怀帕帕·陶马塔·劳

items.title: Britain has made it too easy to become obese - Yahoo
items.body:
原话：“If we are serious about reversing current trends, there is no single intervention that will solve the obesity problem, but several, in combination, could make a meaningful difference.” / “People living with obesity deserve compassionate, evidence-based care rather than judgment.” / “We cannot medicate our way out of an unhealthy food environment.”

items.topic_zh: 肥胖问题的成因与解决方案
items.claim_zh: 肥胖的上升反映了饮食和活动环境的深刻变化，单一干预无法解决这一问题，需要多种措施结合。
items.evidence_zh: 几乎三分之一的英格兰成年人生活在肥胖中，增加了多种疾病的风险。
items.article_body:
Prof Naveed Sattar says the rise in obesity reflects profound changes in how people eat and move - Chris Watt Growing up in Glasgow in the late 1970s, life looked rather different from today. My local shop might have stocked only a handful of biscuit varieties, and a packet was often shared among the family over the course of a week. Most meals were cooked at home, there were far fewer cars on the roads, and many jobs involved considerably more physical activity than is common now.
We should be cautious about romanticising the past. Life was not necessarily better, but in one important respect it was different: the environment in which we lived made it easier to maintain a healthy weight. Daily life involved more movement, and there were far fewer opportunities to consume highly processed , energy-dense foods throughout the day.
Today, the picture is very different. Research I recently co-wrote, led by colleagues at the University of Cambridge, highlights how obesity has become one of the most important public health challenges facing our society. Nearly one in three adults in England now lives with obesity, which increases their risk of many conditions, including type 2 diabetes, cardiovascular disease, liver disease, sleep disorders, several cancers and musculoskeletal conditions, while placing growing pressure on an already stretched NHS.
Perhaps most concerning is that rates are rising faster among younger generations and those living in the most deprived communities. This rise is not a consequence of declining willpower, increased laziness or greater greed. Rather, it reflects profound changes in our food and activity environments that have made weight gain more likely across the population.
If we are serious about reversing current trends, there is no single intervention that will solve the obesity problem, but several, in combination, could make a meaningful difference.
Today, high-calorie foods and drinks are available almost everywhere: supermarkets, petrol stations, high streets and, increasingly, through food-delivery apps. They are heavily marketed, highly convenient and often relatively inexpensive. It is therefore unsurprising that many researchers now regard the food environment as a principal driver of rising obesity rates.
Governments, industry and public health organisations must work together to improve the nutritional quality of the foods available to us. Further legislative restrictions on the marketing of unhealthy products to children, continued reformulation to reduce excess sugar, salt and unhealthy fats, and incentives for companies to develop healthier products should all be pursued.
Improving the nation's health requires a better balance between commercial interests and critically important public health objectives. Ultimately, long-term success will depend on making healthier choices easier and less healthy choices harder.
Eating habits formed in childhood often persist into adulthood. Ensuring access to nutritious school meals can help improve dietary quality, particularly among children from disadvantaged backgrounds who may otherwise bring less nutritious food from home or buy fast food during their lunch break. Ensuring that every child has access to at least one healthier meal every weekday would require investment, but could pay dividends in the long run.
Equally important is practical nutrition education that helps young people understand food, develop cooking skills and appreciate that taste preferences can change over time, so that healthier foods can become highly enjoyable.
Ensuring children have access to nutritious school meals is key to improving dietary quality and instilling healthy eating habits, says Prof Sattar - Chris Watt
New and improved nutrition lessons should be introduced to support children in eating better. We also need more children to train in farming and food processing, so that future generations are interested in producing homegrown British fruit and vegetables. If more of our own produce is available on supermarket shelves, it could be fresher and more appealing, encouraging people to eat more of it. I know this will require investment, but if we want a healthier, fitter, happier nation, it needs to be done.
Physical activity deserves equal attention. Activity levels often fall sharply during adolescence, particularly during the secondary school years. Not every child enjoys competitive sport, and that is entirely reasonable, so schools should actively offer alternatives during PE lessons, such as walking, cycling, dance, outdoor pursuits and recreational games. All contribute to good health.
The goal should not be to create elite athletes; it should be to help young people discover forms of activity they genuinely enjoy. Countries that successfully embed movement throughout the school day, such as the Netherlands, offer useful lessons. Investment in facilities and community partnerships – such as collaborations between schools, leisure centres, charities and local health services to promote healthy eating and physical activity – would be money well spent, delivering benefits for decades to come.
Britain has a growing population of healthy retirees with valuable skills and life experience. With appropriate training, safeguarding and oversight, even occasional volunteering – perhaps once a month – could help support children's physical activity, outdoor learning and community programmes.
Regular movement improves both physical and mental wellbeing, yet around half of adults do not meet the NHS exercise recommendations. Creating communities that encourage activity should therefore be a public health priority. Safe walking and cycling routes and groups, well-maintained parks and green spaces, affordable leisure facilities and community programmes would all help.
Around half of UK adults fail to meet the NHS exercise recommendations
Importantly, opportunities for physical activity are not distributed equally. In affluent areas, people often enjoy better access to safe environments and leisure facilities. In more deprived communities, practical barriers can make regular activity far more difficult. Addressing these inequalities requires sustained local investment.
The public health message itself needs to be simplified. Rather than encouraging only ambitious goals, we should emphasise that even small increases in activity matter. An additional 500 to 1,000 steps a day is achievable for millions of people and could deliver health benefits. Even five to 10 minutes of extra walking each day can help people become more active and can be an achievable starting point.
People living with obesity deserve compassionate, evidence-based care rather than judgment. Obesity is not simply about willpower but is shaped by a complex interplay of genetics, early-life experiences and the environments in which people live, learn and work. People living with obesity should therefore be treated with empathy and respect.
Because obesity affects almost every area of healthcare, all healthcare professionals should receive training in its prevention and management, equipping them with practical lifestyle advice and a clear understanding of the treatments now available, so patients can make informed choices.
Every clinical encounter presents an opportunity to discuss weight sensitively and constructively. In my experience, supported by evidence from trials, most patients are willing to engage when these conversations are approached with empathy and respect.
Glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) injections and tablets have demonstrated substantial weight loss and improvements in a range of obesity-related conditions. By reducing appetite and food cravings, as well as body weight, they give people the opportunity to think about and better adopt other lifestyle changes.
They are not, however, a substitute for obesity prevention. We cannot medicate our way out of an unhealthy food environment. However, they are becoming an increasingly important part of obesity care and offer genuine hope to many people who have struggled with their weight for decades.
The challenge now is ensuring fair and sustainable access. While some worry that private provision may worsen inequalities, there is another perspective. Those who can afford to pay privately may reduce pressure on NHS services, allowing limited public resources to be targeted towards those with the greatest need and the least ability to pay.
The NHS should also begin thinking differently about how these potentially disruptive medicines are managed. Given their likely effect on diabetes, cardiovascular disease, liver disease and multiple other areas of medicine, there is a strong case for a single national body to oversee their implementation, coordinate access and monitor outcomes across the NHS. Such an approach could help ensure consistency, maximise value for money and collate fast real-world evidence of the drugs' effects.
A means-tested co-payment system, whereby some patients contribute towards the cost of treatment according to their ability to pay, could, in principle, stretch finite NHS resources further. This could enable more people to benefit while protecting access for those who would otherwise be unable to afford treatment. Given the scale of the obesity crisis, new approaches to financing effective therapies deserve serious consideration.
There may even be wider societal benefits. As more people use these treatments, demand for healthier foods and smaller portion sizes could encourage manufacturers and retailers to adapt their offerings in ways that benefit the broader population.
These are not the only answers, nor will every proposal prove equally effective, but together they illustrate the breadth of action likely to be needed if we are to give future generations a better chance of living healthier lives.
Professor Naveed Sattar is Professor of Cardiometabolic Medicine at the University of Glasgow and Honorary Consultant at Glasgow Royal Infirmary

items.title_zh: 英国肥胖问题亟需多重干预措施
items.summary_zh: 文章指出，英国肥胖率上升反映了饮食和活动环境的深刻变化，单一的干预措施无法有效解决这一问题。当前，几乎三分之一的英格兰成年人生活在肥胖中，这显著增加了多种疾病的风险。科学家强调，若要逆转这一趋势，必须采取多种措施的结合，而非依赖药物治疗。同时，生活在肥胖中的人们应获得基于证据的关怀，而非评判。
items.l1_lead: 英国肥胖问题日益严重，需综合多重干预措施而非单一药物治疗，以有效应对饮食和活动环境的变化。
items.l2_summary: 英国的肥胖问题日益严重，反映了饮食和活动环境的深刻变化。根据最新数据，几乎三分之一的英格兰成年人正面临肥胖的困扰，这一现象显著增加了多种疾病的风险。科学家们指出，单一的干预措施无法有效应对这一复杂的健康危机，因此必须采取多种措施的结合来逆转这一趋势，而不是单纯依赖药物治疗。当前的研究强调，生活在肥胖中的人们应当获得基于证据的关怀，而不是受到评判和歧视。这种基于证据的关怀不仅能够帮助个体更好地理解自身的健康状况，还能提供有效的支持和指导，促进健康生活方式的形成。综上所述，解决英国肥胖问题需要综合性的干预策略，以应对其背后的多重因素，而非简单依赖单一的解决方案。

items.title: Foundayo: The UK's newest weight loss pill set to be 'much cheaper' than jabs - Metro.co.uk
items.body:
原话：“The arrival of another effective oral option is a positive development and should help more people access treatment that best suits their needs and preferences.”
论点：新的口服减肥药将帮助更多人获得适合他们需求和偏好的治疗。
items.authors: Naveed Sattar
items.attribution_basis: Google News 全名命中 + LLM 同一人核验（Metro.co.uk） + 论点方向独立复核
quotes: The arrival of another effective oral option is a positive development and should help more people access treatment that best suits their needs and preferences.
items.topic_zh: 新口服减肥药的积极影响
items.claim_zh: 新的口服减肥药将帮助更多人获得适合他们需求和偏好的治疗。
items.article_body:
There’s a new kid on the block when it comes to weight loss treatments — and it’s set to give jabs a run for their money.
This week, the UK became the first country in Europe to approve the use of orforglipron — branded as Foundayo — for weight management and type 2 diabetes.
Made by Mounjaro manufacturer Eli Lilly, it’s one of two GLP-1 pills to receive Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency (MHRA) authorisation.
But while it’s got the go-ahead to be sold via private prescription, there’s no indication of whether Foundayo will be offered via the NHS.
Still, many experts are optimistic about the drug, with Dr Simon Cork, senior lecturer in physiology at Anglia Ruskin University, describing it as a ‘big step forward in the treatment of obesity.’
Glasgow University Professor of Metabolic Medicine, Naveed Sattar, added: ‘The arrival of another effective oral option is a positive development and should help more people access treatment that best suits their needs and preferences.’
Like semaglutide and tirzepatide (the active ingredients in Mounjaro, Wegovy and Ozempic ), orforglipron is a GLP-1 receptor agonist, which mimics a naturally occurring hormone, glucagon-like peptide released by the body after eating — just in the form of a pill to be taken once a day.
According to the MHRA, it ‘acts on areas of the brain that regulate appetite, helping people feel fuller for longer, reducing hunger and decreasing food cravings.’
At the same time, the medication regulates blood sugar, making it an effective treatment ‘for patients with insufficiently controlled type 2 diabetes.’
Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.
Foundayo is licensed for adults with insufficiently controlled diabetes, a BMI of 30 or above, or a BMI of between 27 and 30 and at least one weight-related comorbidity such as high blood pressure, heart disease, or obstructive sleep apnoea.
Dr Earim Chaudry, chief medical officer of Voy , tells Metro that people trialled on the highest dose of Foundayo lost an average of 12.4% of their body weight over 72 weeks, with around 1 in 5 participants without diabetes losing at least 20%.

This site is protected by reCAPTCHA and the Google Privacy Policy and Terms of Service apply. Your information will be used in line with our Privacy Policy
Although results aren’t quite as dramatic as with jabs (Mounjaro users lose on average 22.5%) he says the pills can be a good alternative for ‘people who’ve been put off other weight loss medications, either because of needle anxiety or the food restrictions that some oral options require.’
‘Unlike the Wegovy pill, it can be taken at any time of day, with or without food, which offers more flexibility for people who want that,’ Dr Chaudry adds.
The MHRA lists the most common side effects for those taking orforglipron as nausea, constipation, diarrhoea, vomiting, indigestion, and abdominal pain.
Dr Chaudry notes that this is ‘consistent with other GLP-1 weight loss medications’, adding: ‘Stomach issues are common early on with this class of medicine, and tend to settle down as the body gets used to the medication and the dose, especially alongside small lifestyle adjustments.’
Anyone who suspects they’re having a side effect from this medicine is encouraged to talk to their doctor, pharmacist or nurse, and report it directly to the Yellow Card scheme .
While exact pricing may differ when Foundayo becomes available to buy later this month, Dr Simon Cork says it’s ‘likely to be much cheaper than currently available medications.’
Simple Online Pharmacy currently estimates a monthly supply will cost between £100 and £117, depending on dosage, but for those who sign up for a six-month plan with Voy, it’ll start from £69 each month.
In comparison, a minimum dose of Mounjaro currently comes in at £130 to £225 per month (not including introductory subscription discounts), with maintenance doses costing up to £359.
